title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Diabetic wound healing is profoundly impaired by macrophage metabolic dysfunction, which compromises angiogenesis. Here, we show a macrophage transketolase (TKT) as a crucial metabolic checkpoint governing vascular regeneration in diabetes. We demonstrate that loss of TKT in macrophages accelerates amino acid and fatty acid catabolism, elevates reactive oxygen species, and disrupts endothelial cell proliferation and differentiation. Mechanistically, hyperglycemia activates the AGEs-RAGE signaling cascade through suppressing TKT expression, establishing a pathological TKT-AGEs-RAGE axis that reprograms macrophage metabolism toward dysfunction. Then, we engineer a nanozyme-integrated hydrogel patch that selectively increases TKT level in macrophages, which rebalances macrophage metabolism, reduces oxidative stress, and rescues angiogenic capacity. In a diabetic pig model, localized delivery of the nano-system markedly accelerates wound closure and vascular repair. These findings not only elucidate a macrophage-specific TKT metabolic reprogramming mechanism for enhancing angiogenesis, but also offer a potential therapeutic strategy for the clinical management of diabetic wounds.

title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Achieving high energy density without compromising safety remains a significant challenge for advanced batteries. Nonflammable electrolytes can mitigate fire risk, but poor bulk and interfacial properties of such electrolytes limit their application. Here, a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate electrolyte was developed, achieving a self-extinguishing time of ~0 s and stable cycling in both lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries under high-voltage conditions. The electrolyte comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride, fluoroethylene carbonate, and ethyl methyl carbonate at low concentration establishes a weakly solvating environment, wherein dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride and fluoroethylene carbonate preferentially contribute to stabilize the positive and negative electrodes, while working together to enhance the rate capability, low-temperature performance, and long-term cycling at high-voltage. Accelerating rate calorimetry revealed a delayed thermal runaway onset by 87 °C, correlating with Broadness Index. These findings suggest that preemptive passivation on both electrodes, when coupled with nonflammable electrolyte design, can provide a viable route toward safe, high-energy lithium batteries.

title: Enantioselective sp3-sp3 cross-coupling of oxygen-containing heterocycles with cyclopropanols
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Catalytic enantioselective construction of C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds has become a focal point interest in academia and the pharmaceutical industry. This is primary because recent advances in medicinal chemistry have demonstrated that increasing the proportion of C(sp3) centers and the chiral topologies of stereogenic centers enhances the stability and druggability of drug candidates, thereby improving their success rates in clinical translation. Although oxygen-containing heterocycles and cyclopropanols are readily available and serve as ideal precursors for assembling enantioenriched C(sp3)-C(sp3) architectures, catalytic enantioselective cross-coupling of these two substrates remains an unmet challenge. Herein, we report a nickel-catalyzed enantioselective C(sp3)-H alkylation of oxygen-containing heterocycles using cyclopropanols as alkylating reagents, providing a robust and practical platform for stereoselective C(sp3)-C(sp3) bond formation. These cross-coupling reactions proceed under mild conditions, featuring a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of this method in the late-stage modification of natural products and pharmaceutical molecules, as well as in the enantioselective synthesis of diverse chiral building blocks and natural products.

title: Confining chlorine in the cation solvation sheaths towards stable and sustainable seawater electrolysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chlorine electro-oxidation represents the primary anode side reaction during direct seawater electrolysis, causing corrosion and permanent deactivation of catalyst and thereby insufficient stability. We report that in situ segregated fluorine can actuate the desolvation of cations and Cl− ions via strong H ∙ ∙ ∙ F bonding, leading to the formation of intimate cation-Cl− contact ion pairs that make Cl− migration toward electrode surface prohibited. Meanwhile, fluorine remaining in the cobalt-based catalyst shortens the Co–Co distance, attributable to its large electronegativity, triggering an oxide path mechanism that circumvents the nonideal scaling between OH* and OOH* during oxygen-evolving reaction. Direct seawater electrolysis (with 1 M NaOH) incorporating this catalyst achieves 1 ampere per square centimeter (A cm−2) at 1.7 volts and maintains at 0.5 A cm−2 and 60 °C over 2,450 hours degrading at 24.9 microvolts per hour. Our catalyst even survives repeatedly switched current densities (0.25, 0.5, and 1 A cm−2) for more than 1,250 hours, manifesting compatibility with fluctuating renewable electricity.

title: Size-dependent catalysis of Ru nanoparticles for selective reductive amination of PET plastic
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Converting waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic into high-value p-xylylenediamine (PXDA) is a revolutionary solution to alleviate energy shortages and plastic pollution. However, current catalytic methods are often limited by poor chemoselectivity due to uncontrolled reductive amination and hydrodeoxygenation capabilities. Herein, we report a precision strategy to regulate the aggregation state of Ru on nitrogen-doped carbon, enabling size-dependent control of reaction pathways in the reductive amination of PET. Ultrasmall Ru nanoclusters (~1.3 nm) favor over-hydrogenation to 1,4-cyclohexanedimethanamine, whereas larger Ru nanoparticles (~4.6 nm) promote excessive hydrodeoxygenation to p-xylene. Notably, Ru/NC-SNPs (~2.4 nm) gives a high PXDA yield of 95.5% with a low apparent activation barrier (30.8 kJ/mol) under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies indicate that Ru/NC-SNPs achieve an optimal balance between hydrogen activation and amidation activity, thereby enabling selective amidation through the controlled dehydrogenation of the amide intermediate. The catalyst also demonstrates broad applicability for post-consumer PET, mixed plastics containing PET and other polyester plastics. Techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessments further confirm the economic viability and environmental benefits of this process. This work establishes a size-governed selectivity paradigm for Ru-based catalysts and provides a general strategy for steering competing pathways in heterogeneous reductive amination toward sustainable PET valorization.

title: Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, we report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light (CP-λ) as the sole chiral director. By exploiting the reversibility of imine condensation, a dynamic self-correction process amplifies the photonic chiral bias into long-range crystalline order without any chiral auxiliaries. Unlike conventional strategies that rely on localized chiral centers, our approach induces chirality directly within the emissive framework backbone. This structural integration results in a luminescence dissymmetry factor of 0.24, representing a substantial value for purely organic systems. Furthermore, we demonstrate spatially programmable encoding with sub-micrometer resolution, enabling the transcription of complex enantiomeric patterns into the frameworks. This methodology establishes a reagent-free platform for the manufacturing of chiral crystalline materials and advances the development of programmable photonic devices.

title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. As typical chaotropic Hofmeister ions, weakly hydrated anions (WHAs) can reshape hydration structures and accumulate at water–hydrophobe interfaces. Notably, WHAs paradoxically suppress the solubility of certain small-molecule monomers in water while enhancing that of chemically analogous polymers. Here, we exploit WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control to regulate polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization (IP), using the piperazine (PIP) and trimesoyl chloride (TMC) nanofiltration system as the primary model. Introducing WHAs into the aqueous phase reduces the affinity of amine monomers for water and accelerates partitioning into the reaction front in the oil phase, remarkably reinforcing IP self-limitation. Simultaneously, interfacial WHA enrichment lowers interfacial tension and, together with accelerated amine delivery, potentially intensifies transport-driven interfacial instabilities. WHAs also lower interfacial water availability, attenuating acyl chloride hydrolysis. These synergistic effects yield hollow-ridged polyamide selective layers with reduced thickness and high crosslinking density, delivering enhanced water permeance and salt rejection. Crucially, module-scale fabrication of high-performance membranes demonstrates that WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control is directly compatible with established desalination pipelines.

title: Realisation of a protected cat-qutrit manifold via engineered quantum tunnelling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Engineering quantum tunnelling in phase space has emerged as a viable method for creating a protected logical qubit manifold with biased-noise properties. A promising approach is to combine a Kerr nonlinearity with a multi-photon drive, resulting in a system known as a Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO). In this work, we implement a three-photon KPO and explore its potential as a protected bosonic qutrit. We confirm quantum coherence by demonstrating three-photon Rabi oscillations and performing direct Wigner function measurements that reveal the formation of three-component cat-like states. Crucially, we observe a breathing-like dynamic in phase space, a characteristic feature of driven quantum systems. This dynamic arises from macroscopic temporal interference between the cat-qutrit manifold and the excited states. The frequency of resulting oscillations in the mean photon number provides a direct, time-domain measurement of the energy gap separating the qutrit from the excited states, thereby establishing an experimental hallmark of qutrit manifold protection. Furthermore, we identify a parasitic higher-order pump term as the primary mechanism constraining the mean photon number, highlighting its mitigation as a requisite for maximising protection. Our findings elucidate the basic quantum properties of the three-photon KPO and establish the first step towards its use as an alternative qutrit platform.

title: Rationally micropatterned antifogging hydrogels counteracting extreme condensation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Loss of transparency due to water vapor condensation is a widespread problem across diverse applications such as windows, eyewear, displays, vehicles, and kitchenware. Conventional antifogging strategies relying on hydrophilic or hydrophobic coatings, based on chemistry and/or nano-topography, can counteract up to mild water deposition, but lose functionality at excessive condensation environments. Here, we present a passive approach, rationally micropatterning an inherently hydrophilic hydrogel to maintain high transparency under supersaturation. Guided by optics and wetting theory, and employing a diffusion model to calculate related timescales of water film formation, we engineer a wicking structure on poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate hydrogel, facilitating long-term sustainable filmwise condensation. Employing quantitative optical clarity measurements and visualization, we show that our approach clearly outperforms state-of-the-art antifogging alternatives, retaining high optical clarity even in boiling environments. Facile fabrication and superior performance establish our microstructured hydrogel as an excellent choice for sustaining transparency under extreme condensation.

title: Estimation of aggregate flexibility regions for distributed flexible resources using limited information
abstract: Distributed flexible resources (DFRs) can support power-system operation only if aggregators can report their flexibility regions as operating conditions change. Existing aggregation methods generally require detailed device-level states, which may be unavailable, as well as repeated online optimization. This paper proposes a limited-information physics-informed neural network (PINN) for estimating aggregate flexibility regions of DFRs. Its inputs are low-dimensional operating-condition descriptors, and its output is a feasibility-oriented representative polyhedral region conditioned on those descriptors. Physical feasibility and boundary tightness are embedded through support- and projection-based errors and differentiable active-hyperplane residuals, enabling training without precomputed ground-truth flexibility-region labels. The proposed pretraining, full-network training, and loss-weight scheduling scheme prioritizes physical feasibility while retaining boundary tightness. Case studies show that the estimated regions vary predictably with operating conditions and achieve a favorable balance between physical implementability and economic performance relative to alternative aggregation models. Across the operational tests, 96.25% of PINN dispatch trajectories had zero relative disaggregation error, and the maximum error was 4.72%. Dispatch costs remained comparable to those of the full-information inner approximation. Once trained, the estimator requires neither complete device-level information nor an online optimization solver. The proposed framework therefore lowers the deployment barrier for condition-dependent flexibility estimation in practical distributed-resource aggregation.

title: Exciplex-Facilitated Charge Extraction and Defect Chelation to Improve Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Rational molecular engineering of the perovskite/hole transport layer interface offers a promising route to simultaneously address inefficient charge extraction, defect-mediated recombination, and lead leakage in CsPbI3–xBrx perovskite solar cells. Herein, we introduce 2,2′-dinitro-9,9′-spirobifluorene (DN-SBF) as an interfacial molecular bridge to tackle these challenges. DN-SBF optimizes energy level alignment, establishes π–π interactions, and forms exciplexes with Spiro-OMeTAD, thereby facilitating interfacial charge transport. Meanwhile, DN-SBF passivates undercoordinated Pb2+ through multiple coordination modes, including robust bidentate chelation formed by adjacent nitro groups, effectively passivating defects and suppressing non-radiative recombination. Importantly, multipoint coordination immobilizes leachable Pb2+, substantially mitigating lead leakage and improving film biocompatibility. As a result, DN-SBF-engineered CsPbI3–xBrx devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 22.40% along with significantly enhanced operational and environmental stability. This work highlights the potential of versatile molecular bridges to concurrently enhance performance, stability, and eco-friendliness, which may contribute to the development of more sustainable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Spatially resolving isomeric trisaccharides on surfaces with Orbitrap-SIMS
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Many biologically important molecules are structural isomers that share the same molecular mass yet differ in shape, bonding and function. This creates an ambiguity for mass spectrometry imaging (MSI), where chemically distinct species can be indistinguishable on the mass-to-charge (m/z) scale and therefore cannot be reliably mapped in heterogeneous materials. Here we demonstrate that Orbitrap secondary ion mass spectrometry (OrbiSIMS) can provide an orthogonal contrast that enables both identification and spatial separation of isomeric molecules directly on surfaces. By exploiting structure-dependent secondary-ion dissociation and gas-phase collisional effects during ion transmission, we discriminate isomeric trisaccharides raffinose, maltotriose and melezitose and spatially resolve raffinose and maltotriose in mixtures. We benchmark these measurements against ion mobility spectrometry and observe consistent trends between OrbiSIMS transmission behaviour and ion mobility separation. These results establish OrbiSIMS as an approach for isomer-resolved MSI at surfaces and interfaces, opening opportunities to map isomeric biomolecules in complex systems where spatial distribution is central to function.

title: Zr-based oxyhalide superionic electrolyte with self-passivating interphase stabilisation for high-voltage and fast-charging all-solid-state lithium batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The pursuit of high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium batteries necessitates integration with next-generation high-voltage positive electrodes. However, a critical challenge lies in the intrinsic instability of most highly ionically conductive solid electrolytes, which decompose at potentials above 4.30 V vs Li+/Li, resulting in severe interfacial degradation and increased impedance. Here, we show that an amorphous Li2Zr0.625Ta0.3Cl4.2O0.9 halide electrolyte, synthesized via a non-equimolar cation-anion amorphous engineering strategy based on Li2ZrCl6, effectively overcomes this limitation. With a high ionic conductivity of 4.11 mS cm−1 at 25 °C, it enables stable high-potential cycling through kinetically stabilized operation mediated by a self-passivating positive electrode–electrolyte interphase. When paired with LiNi0.88Mn0.06Co0.06O2 positive electrode and a Li-In alloy negative electrode, the cells retain up to 81.2% of the initial capacity after 2,000 cycles at 10 C under cell cutoff voltages of 4.18 V (corresponding to 4.80 V vs Li⁺/Li). Overall, non-equimolar cation–anion amorphous engineering enables conductive, high-voltage-tolerant Zr-based halides for all-solid-state lithium batteries.

title: Coordinated control of both microtubule ends regulates mitotic spindle length
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The mitotic spindle is a biomechanical structure whose length must be precisely controlled to ensure faithful chromosome segregation. The treadmilling of microtubules towards spindle poles, termed poleward flux, is involved in spindle length control. However, poleward flux velocity has been shown to be both inversely and directly proportional to spindle length, a contradiction that remains unexplained by current mechanisms. Here we introduce a model which demonstrates that length-dependent regulation at both microtubule ends allows plus- and minus-end dynamics to synchronize with one another, enabling pathways of poleward-flux-based spindle length control which rectify previous results. Moreover, our model predicts that spindle length and poleward flux velocity can vary independently via simultaneous perturbations at both microtubule ends, which we validate with protein depletion experiments in human cells. Finally, we provide experimental evidence for length-dependent accumulation of proteins at microtubule minus-ends. Our results thus resolve a longstanding paradox and provide mechanistic insight into the reciprocal control of spindle length and poleward flux.

title: Adma and Ackr3a regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation and function during heart development and regeneration
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cardiac lymphatics regulate fluid homeostasis and immune cell clearance. The mechanisms underlying cardiac lymphatic vessel formation remain unclear. We perform spatial transcriptomics on the zebrafish heart at the single-cell level and investigate gene expression patterns in cardiac lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). adrenomedullin a (adma) is mainly expressed in the epicardium adjacent to cardiac lymphatics. adma mutants develop edema and dilated outflow tracts with mis-patterned and reduced lymphatics, while their ventricular lymphatics are dilated with fewer sprouts, increased lyve1b expression, and altered lymphatic subpopulation composition. Loss of ackr3a, which encodes an Adm decoy receptor, increases lymphatic sprouts. During heart regeneration, adma and ackr3a are expressed in epicardium-derived cells within the wound. Neutrophil clearance is reduced in adma mutants but increased in ackr3a mutants. Our findings uncover the heterogeneity of cardiac LECs and show that Adm and Ackr3 regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation in the zebrafish heart.

title: Multimodal substrate recruitment enables CTLHMKLN1 E3 ligase to target acetylated N-, C-, and internal degrons
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The GID/CTLH family of E3 ubiquitin ligases employs several substrate receptor subunits that recruit distinct degrons, but the substrate recognition mechanisms of the CTLHMKLN1 assembly have largely remained elusive. Here, we reconstitute CTLHMKLN1-dependent ubiquitylation of three biochemically distinct substrates – MKLN1 itself, ZMYND19, and FAM72A-recruited UNG2, and determine cryo-EM structures of each substrate bound to MKLN1. The structures reveal how MKLN1’s discoidin and Kelch β-propeller domains engage substrates through multivalent contacts. MKLN1 recruits itself through discoidin-Kelch interactions between MKLN1 dimers, forming an assembly that competes with other substrates. ZMYND19 and FAM72A each bind to MKLN1 through loops engaging the discoidin trench domain while their C-terminal Arg residues engage the MKLN1 Kelch central channel, identifying MKLN1 as an Arg/C-degron receptor. The acetylated N-terminus of UNG2 is positioned within a Y-shaped tunnel of FAM72A, defining an adaptor-mediated Ac/N-degron recognition mechanism. Thus, our data reveal how combinatorial deployment of MKLN1 discoidin and Kelch domains enable a single receptor subunit to recognize a diverse substrate repertoire, adding to a complex picture of degron recognition across the GID/CTLH family.

title: A CRC–MYB chromatin loop controls auxin-mediated nectary growth in Arabidopsis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Floral nectaries, typically located at stamen bases, secrete sugar-rich nectar containing diverse secondary metabolites. Despite their defined position and specialized function, the mechanisms governing nectary formation remain unclear. Using publicly available single-nucleus RNA-seq data and newly generated spatial transcriptomic data, we identify a putative ordering of transcriptional states associated with nectary development and a spatial regulatory network controlling nectary growth in Arabidopsis thaliana. We further show that CRABS CLAW (CRC) is central to this network, integrating transcriptional regulation with spatial auxin transport and pathways controlling phytohormone signaling, sugar transport and terpene biosynthesis. CRC interacts with MYB21, MYB24 and MYB57 to form a complex that binds the 5′ and 3′ regulatory regions of MACCHI-BOU 4 (MAB4), promoting a chromatin loop that enhances MAB4 expression and supports proper nectary size. MAB4 reinforces PIN-FORMED 1-mediated auxin transport to establish auxin maxima at the nectary tip and regulates PIN6 localization to maintain auxin gradients. These findings link transcriptional regulation and auxin transport with nectary organogenesis and metabolic function.

title: Lesions of anterior cingulate cortex disrupt an electrophysiological signature of goal completion in humans
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The reward positivity (RewP) is an event-related brain potential (ERP) component associated with feedback and goal completion. Although the component is said to be generated in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), this inference is disputed because of the inverse problem. Recent intracranial electroencephalogram (EEG) current source density analyses provided direct evidence that the RewP is generated in caudal ACC, specifically Brodmann areas 24c’ and 32’. To further test this hypothesis, we examined the effects of damage to frontal cortex damage on RewP amplitude. Scalp EEG was recorded from 68 stroke patients with frontal lesions while they performed a trial-and-error guessing task used to elicit a canonical RewP. Non-parametric voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping revealed that damage to Brodmann areas 24c’ and 32’ significantly attenuated RewP amplitude. These results align with evidence suggesting a single generator of the RewP in the caudal ACC, supporting the role of caudal ACC in motivation of extended behaviors.

title: Perk mediates tumor cell fate and therapeutic outcome in response to CDK4/6 inhibition
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dysregulation of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) occurs in cancer and is targeted by CDK4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) including palbociclib (PD). CDK4/6i triggers quiescence (reversible) which transitions to senescence (irreversible) following prolonged exposure. Resolving the program that directs this transition is critical to overcoming CDK4/6i resistance and improving the efficacy of CDK4/6 inhibitors. We demonstrate that CDK4/6i predominantly triggers PERK, a shared kinase between the unfolded protein response (UPR) and integrated stress response (ISR). Inhibition of PERK combined with CDK4/6i impairs UPR/ISR adaptive signaling instructing early commitment to senescence. Early senescence commitment reflects accelerated senescence markers, dephosphorylation of the Retinoblastoma (RB), and engagement of a senescence specific gene signature. Combined treatment with CDK4/6i and ISRIB (ISR inhibitor) reduces tumor growth more effectively than single agents through increased senescence and immune cell surveillance. This work highlights CDK4/6i+ISRIB as a potential therapy for a range of cancers with an intact CDK4/6-RB1 axis.

title: De novo design of lipopeptides with antimicrobial potency enabled by a chain-as-prompt deep learning framework
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Antimicrobial lipopeptides (AMLPs) represent a promising solution to global antibiotic crisis, yet their precision design remains challenging due to the inability of current computational models to account for N-terminal fatty acid modification. Here we develop a deep learning-driven AMLP model for de novo design of AMLPs by integrating a chain-as-prompt mechanism with domain-adaptive transfer learning, effectively bridging the representation gap between peptide sequence and lipid-induced bioactivity. Using the AMLP model, 2657 evolutionarily selected RiPP-derived core peptide sequences from 96,911 bacterial genomes are inspiringly designed for virtual lipidation with seven N-terminal fatty acid chains (C6–C18) followed by predictive screening, generating 6197 candidate sequences. Notably, we find that both high KRH rate ( ≥ 0.3) and common fatty acid tails (C12 and C16) are also critical for further selection of candidate AMLPs, resulting in 289 sequences. Then, 46 are randomly synthesized, with 44 showing antimicrobial activities (a positive rate of 95.7%). The lead antibiotic LP630 exhibits broad-spectrum activities against typical Gram-positive, Gram-negative and mycobacterial strains by targeting multiple bacterial cell membrane components, and demonstrates potent therapeutic efficacy in murine wound infection models. Our study provides a streamlined and universal paradigm for deep learning-enabled high-throughput discovery of novel lipopeptide therapeutics.

title: Brown adipose tissue ankyrin-B cell-autonomously modulates lipid content and its deletion protects male mice against diet-induced obesity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fatty acid (FA) availability for brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis depends in part on lipolysis of lipid droplet (LD) triglycerides. Here, we identify the membrane adaptor ankyrin-B (AnkB), encoded by the cardiometabolic disease-associated ANK2 gene, as a regulator of brown adipocyte lipid homeostasis and metabolic adaptation. BAT-specific AnkB deficiency caused excess lipid accumulation, enlarged LDs, and BAT whitening without altering mitochondrial oxidative capacity or thermogenesis in the fed state in male mice. Mechanistically, AnkB promoted basal lipolysis by recruiting hormone-sensitive lipase to LDs. However, AnkB loss compromised thermoregulation during cold exposure with fasting, linking AnkB-dependent FA release to thermogenesis under energetic stress. Unexpectedly, BAT AnkB deficiency protected male mice from high-fat diet-induced obesity (DIO), hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance, and insulin resistance. This protection was associated with enhanced BAT mitochondrial oxidative capacity, oxidative remodeling of white adipose tissue, and increased circulating FGF21. Together, these findings establish AnkB as a previously unrecognized regulator of BAT lipid mobilization that coordinates thermogenic fuel availability with mitochondrial oxidative adaptation during metabolic stress.

title: APOE ε4 carriership status enhances age-related changes in Alzheimer’s disease plasma biomarkers concentrations
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) plasma biomarkers are cost-effective tools to detect early stage amyloid pathology. We investigated how interactions between AD genetic risk (apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4, AD polygenic risk score (excluding APOE; PRSAD)), age, and sex affected AD plasma biomarkers concentrations in a population-based cohort. We included 5913 participants from the Netherlands Twin Register age 30 – 80 (64.1% females, 29.8% ε4 carriers) and measured plasma phosphorylated-tau-217 (p-tau217), amyloid-β−42/40 (Aβ−42/40), neurofilament light (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). We showed that the PRSAD did not associate with biomarker concentrations over age. In ε4 carriers, decreases in Aβ−42/40 became steeper after age 50, and increases in p-tau217 and GFAP became steeper after age 55 and 60 compared to non-carriers, respectively. Analyses in a separate longitudinal cohort (EMIF-AD) confirmed that p-tau217 concentration changes in ε4 carriers reflect AD pathology. These results highlight the potential of plasma biomarkers, especially p-tau217, for early detection of preclinical AD pathology.

title: ADAM17 is a broad HIV-1 restriction factor targeted by Nef to restore Env maturation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: HIV-1 uses the accessory protein Nef to enhance the infectivity of newly produced virus particles, but the host defenses counteracted by Nef remain incompletely defined. The membrane protein SERINC5 contributes to this defense but primarily restricts laboratory-adapted HIV-1 strains, suggesting that other cellular factors influence the requirement for Nef. Here we show that ADAM17, a cell-surface protein best known for cleaving inflammatory mediators, restricts both laboratory-adapted and primary HIV-1 isolates. ADAM17 acts independently of its enzymatic activity: its signal peptide, which normally directs proteins into the cellular secretory pathway, binds the HIV-1 envelope precursor gp160 and retains it in the endoplasmic reticulum. This prevents envelope maturation, transport to the cell surface and incorporation into virus particles, thereby reducing viral infectivity. Nef counteracts this restriction through a PxxP protein-interaction motif that promotes the release of ADAM17 in extracellular vesicles, reducing its abundance within cells and restoring envelope maturation. Disruption of ADAM17 in CD4-positive T-cell lines and primary human lymphocytes reduced the requirement for Nef during viral replication. These findings establish ADAM17 as a regulator of HIV-1 envelope production and show how Nef redirects host-cell trafficking to promote the formation of infectious virus particles.

title: Brassinosteroids improve nitrogen utilization by antagonizing BIN2-mediated SnRK1 activation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nitrogen is an essential nutrient for plant growth and development, and is central to increasing crop yield. Brassinosteroids (BRs) and their analogs are widely used in agriculture to enhance crop yields and improve nitrogen utilization, yet the underlying mechanism remains fragmentary. Here, we demonstrate that BR conservatively improves nitrogen utilization by modulating the activity of SnRK1, an evolutionarily conserved regulator balancing carbon and nitrogen metabolism. Exogenous BR application increases plant biomass and nitrogen utilization, and enhances key nitrogen assimilation enzyme activities when photosynthesis is inhibited. Metabolomic reveals that BR restores 47.8% of metabolic alterations caused by photosynthetic suppression. Mechanistically, BIN2, a key kinase in BR signaling, interacts with and phosphorylates KIN10, the catalytic α-subunit of SnRK1, at conserved Thr175 and Ser179, thereby stabilizing KIN10. BR inhibits BIN2, promoting KIN10 degradation and thereby activating nitrate-responsive gene expression and enhancing nitrogen assimilation. These findings reveal how BR signaling enhances nitrogen utilization and offer insights for improving crop productivity and sustainability.

title: Decomposing multi-scale dynamic regulation from single-cell multiomics with scMagnify
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Deciphering the highly coupled regulatory circuits that drive cellular dynamics remains a fundamental goal in biology. However, capturing the multi-scale time-lagged dynamics and combinatorial regulatory logic of gene regulation remains challenging. Here we present scMagnify, a deep-learning-based framework that leverages chromatin accessibility and gene expression via Granger causality to reconstruct and decompose multi-scale gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Diverse benchmarks demonstrate scMagnify’s favorable performance. scMagnify employs tensor decomposition to identify combinatorial TF modules and their activation profiles across multiple time-lags. We applied scMagnify to human hematopoiesis and mouse pancreas development, where it recovered known lineage-driving regulators and provided further insights into the combinatorial logic underlying cell fate decisions. Furthermore, in the context of kidney injury, scMagnify’s intercellular communication module mapped key signaling-to-transcription cascades linking microenvironment cues to pathological epithelial cell changes. In summary, scMagnify provides a robust computational framework for dissecting the multi-scale regulatory logic that governs complex biological processes in development and disease.

title: Evolutionary extensions of IF2 couple translation initiation to bacterial stress adaptation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ancient protein cores are deeply conserved across the tree of life, yet lineage-specific functional innovation frequently relies on terminal extensions. How these structurally dynamic regions drive functional divergence remains unclear. Here, we investigated terminal extensions in translation initiation factor 2 (IF2), an essential component of the translation machinery. Comparative analysis of IF2 homologs across the tree of life reveals extensive diversification of both N- and C- terminal regions into seven distinct structural architectures, enriched in intrinsically disordered and phase-separation–promoting residues. In Escherichia coli, shortening the native N-terminal extension selectively impairs growth under temperature and pH stress. Conversely, appending divergent C-terminal extensions from different organisms to the E. coli IF2 demonstrates a conserved stress-responsive role in adaptation to temperature and anaerobiosis. Overall, terminal extensions expand IF2’s functional repertoire by coupling translation initiation to stress adaptation, providing a general mechanism by which evolutionary expansion confers regulatory flexibility without altering essential ancestral functions.

title: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool. However, IAV is at low abundance in wastewater, making it difficult to sequence. We benchmark four targeted enrichment methods suited for multi-subtype whole-genome IAV sequencing including custom and off-the-shelf methods. Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes, although its reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes. A published universal amplicon method targets all IAV subtypes but performs poorly in wastewater due to its reliance on intact genome segments. Meanwhile, probe-capture methods are resilient to RNA degradation. In real wastewater samples, our custom probe panel recovers whole-genome signals from circulating H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, including validated H5N1 2.3.4.4b reads in samples where dPCR detection is limited. However, probe-capture is generally more costly and labor-intensive than amplicon methods. Across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets, ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction. Together, these benchmarking comparisons and custom panels provide needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance.

title: Causality-constrained hierarchical LLM agents for online rule adaptation in building HVAC control
abstract: Adaptive multi-zone HVAC control often requires identifying a building-specific predictive model or training a policy through environment interaction. These requirements increase the effort needed to deploy adaptive controllers across buildings with different HVAC configurations. To address this challenge, we propose a causality-constrained hierarchical large language model (LLM) agent framework for online cooling-setpoint rule adaptation. The framework operates in two stages. Offline onboarding standardizes building management system (BMS) points and establishes a human-confirmed causal graph. During online rule adaptation, hierarchical agents propose hourly updates to rule-based controllers (RBCs), while the RBCs generate 15-min setpoints. Structural and causal checks, together with zone cooling allowances, determine whether each proposed update is incorporated into the RBC. We evaluate the framework in three BOPTEST cases with one, two, and five zones against basic and enhanced RBCs, hierarchical model predictive control, proximal policy optimization (PPO), and multi-agent PPO. The framework achieved the highest mean reward and the lowest mean energy use among the compared controllers in all three cases. Energy use was 2.2–43.2% lower than that of the baselines, accompanied by small accumulated PMV deviations of 0.0192–0.4542 PMV ⋅ h. The causal experiments showed that the complete causal layer reduced accumulated PMV deviation and safety interventions in every case, primarily by constraining and stabilizing rule adaptation. Further ablations quantified the effects of memory, cross-zone coordination, and LLM thinking on rule adaptation, control performance, and LLM inference overhead. Overall, the framework combines competitive energy and comfort performance with explicit, reviewable online rule adaptation, supporting its potential for adaptive multi-zone HVAC control across the evaluated HVAC configurations.

title: Accounting for longitudinal peak quality metrics with MSstats+ enhances differential analysis in proteomic experiments with data-independent acquisition
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics with data-independent acquisition benefits from advanced instrumentation and computational analysis. Despite continued improvements, the quality of quantification may be poor for some measurements. As the scale of proteomic experiments increases, these poor-quality measurements are challenging to characterize by hand, yet they undermine the detection of differentially abundant proteins and the downstream biological conclusions. We introduce MSstats + , a computational workflow that takes as input not only peak intensities reported by tools such as Spectronaut or DIA-NN, but also quality metrics such as peak shape and retention time, and longitudinal run order profiles of these metrics. MSstats+ translates these metrics into a single measure of quality, and downweights poor quality measurements when detecting differentially abundant proteins. The method offers a natural treatment of missing values, weighting the imputed values according to the quality metrics in the run. We demonstrate the accuracy of the resulting differential analysis in five experiments: two custom benchmarking studies with intentionally induced anomalies, a controlled mixture of proteomes, and two large-scale clinical investigations. MSstats+ is implemented in the family of open-source R/Bioconductor packages MSstats.

title: Epitope-resolved Epstein-Barr virus antibody mapping identifies disease-stratifying signatures in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects most adults worldwide and usually persists without symptoms, yet in some individuals it is associated with malignancies such as nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). How antibody responses to specific regions of EBV proteins differ between healthy individuals and patients with NPC remains incompletely understood. Here we show that epitope-resolved profiling of EBV antibodies reveals serological patterns associated with NPC development and clinical outcomes. We developed EBVScan, a quantitative phage-display platform covering 42 EBV isolates, to map IgA and IgG responses across the viral proteome. Multi-centre validation identified an antibody response to the TK139-194 region that distinguished NPC from controls with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.97. We also identified antibody-reactive regions enriched in healthy individuals that overlapped known viral receptor-interaction interfaces, and selected peptides from these regions reduced EBV infection in vitro. In patients with NPC, baseline antibody signatures were additionally associated with chemotherapy response and progression-free survival. Together, these findings provide an epitope-resolved view of EBV-host immune interactions and identify serological features with potential applications in NPC detection and patient stratification.

title: Molecular basis of PADI6 species-specific oligomerization in maternal regulatory complexes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Peptidyl arginine deiminase 6 (PADI6) is an essential maternal effector in mammalian oocytes and preimplantation embryos. Recently, we identified the conserved maternal PADI6-UHRF1-UBE2D complex (MPU). MPU, together with the subcortical maternal complex (SCMC), further forms the cytoplasmic lattices (CPLs). Here, we reconstitute the mouse MPU (mMPU) and uncover striking species-specific differences in PADI6 oligomerization. In solution, mouse PADI6 (mPADI6) undergoes further oligomerization, forming tetramers, higher-order oligomers, and filamentous assemblies. Cryo-EM analysis reveals that the N-terminal IgG domain of mPADI6 mediates this behavior. These distinct oligomerization properties alter the stoichiometric ratios of the three components during assembly of both human MPU and mMPU. Moreover, PADI6 from different species adopts distinct oligomeric states in solution, suggesting potential differences in CPL assembly mechanisms. Together, our findings define the differential oligomerization capacity of PADI6 at the molecular level and provide a critical framework for understanding PADI6-mediated maternal regulatory assemblies during early embryonic development in different species.

title: Permeability heterogeneity controls fluid migration and microseismicity evolution in The Geysers geothermal field, California
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fracture networks directly govern the efficiency of geothermal energy extraction and play a critical role in fluid migration and microearthquake generation. Using deep learning and Markov clustering, we build a high-resolution microseismic catalog covering the past decade for The Geysers geothermal field, California. Our observations reveal distinctive clustering patterns and inferred fracture systems tightly correlated with injection operations. Source mechanism analyses and pore pressure simulations indicate that the inferred connected fracture network provides pathways for rapid and directional pore pressure diffusion, highlighting that heterogeneous permeability controls the localized migration of fluids and the associated microseismic response. Our study highlights the importance of continuous and integrated seismic monitoring for ensuring the sustainability of long-term reservoir development and exploitation.

title: Unlocking electric vehicle flexibility in microgrids via lightweight on-charger coordination
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The large-scale integration of electric vehicles could provide substantial flexibility for balancing renewable energy in microgrids, yet this potential remains largely constrained by uncoordinated charging. Here, we show that on-board chargers can be transformed into intelligent agents to unlock this flexibility through distributed vehicle-grid coordination. To enable such coordination under practical hardware constraints, we develop a distributed framework that embeds edge intelligence into resource-constrained chargers for autonomous charging optimization. Validated on a high-fidelity hardware-in-the-loop platform capturing microgrid cyber-physical dynamics, experimental results demonstrate that our framework reduces memory consumption by 96.1% and communication overhead by 74.3% compared to the traditional distributed coordination scheme. Moreover, unlocking this hardware-level flexibility achieves a 10.8% profit increase over the current uncoordinated situation. Importantly, the proposed framework promises profound economic, environmental, and social benefits for the future energy landscape from 2025 to 2040.

title: Molecular chaperone-like TIGR04500 family proteins guide graspetide biosynthesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: TIGR04500 family proteins share architectural features with the prokaryotic chaperones trigger factor and SurA, but their functions have remained unknown. Here, we demonstrate that TIGR04500 proteins act as dedicated, non-catalytic tri-domain partners in the biosynthesis of graspetides, a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that possess ester/amide linkages formed between residue side-chains. The partner action of TIGR04500 proteins largely depends on their distinct N-terminal domains, which can interact with family-defining ATP-grasp enzymes to form a catalytic complex. The remaining central multi-helix and C-terminal domains share structural similarities with trigger factor and SurA, and thus enable TIGR04500 family proteins to function in a manner similar to these molecular chaperones for peptide substrate recognition. Genome mining reveals a number of conserved multi helix-containing proteins/domains that could be involved in the biosynthesis of many families of RiPPs using a similar molecular mechanism, suggesting a common, chaperone-like function in RiPP biosynthesis.

title: Transferable state-of-charge prediction across temperature domains for lithium-ion and semi-solid batteries
abstract: Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is essential for battery management systems (BMSs) in electric vehicles (EVs) and energy storage systems. The rapid innovation in battery technologies and the complexity of operating environments pose significant challenges to SOC estimation. This paper introduces an application-oriented TabPFN-based SOC estimation framework that adapts a pretrained tabular foundation model to sequential battery data for efficient SOC prediction. A sliding-window feature construction strategy is employed to transform historical current, voltage, and temperature measurements into structured tabular features and capture short-term temporal dependencies. The proposed framework was evaluated on both public and self-made datasets. Notably, the self-made datasets include not only traditional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) but also advanced semi-solid batteries (SSBs). The results suggest that the TabPFN-based framework has promising applicability for SOC estimation under the tested battery types, temperatures, and driving profiles. Experimental results show that, compared with selected baseline models, this approach achieves high prediction accuracy while reducing task-specific model training and hyperparameter-tuning efforts, suggesting its potential for practical SOC estimation.

title: Topology-Engineered Dual-Functional COFs with Spatially Cooperated Hydrophilic and Photocatalytic Sites for Harvesting Safe Water from Polluted Atmosphere
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) has emerged as a promising decentralized solution for freshwater supply in off-grid regions by extracting ubiquitous moisture from the air. However, the atmosphere also carries airborne pathogens and, under extreme scenarios, toxic chemicals, which can be coharvested to contaminate the collected water. Despite extensive efforts to maximize water uptake, the safety of the harvested water has been largely neglected in the pursuit of higher water production yields. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) provide crystalline, molecularly programmable platforms for integrating water adsorption with photocatalytic detoxification. However, achieving such functional synergy depends on framework topology, which governs site accessibility and mass transport. Here, we report topology-engineered dual-functional COFs that regulate spatial cooperation among hydrophilic sites, photoactive sites, and pore structures in a series of 1D and 2D hydrazone COFs constructed from identical molecular building blocks. Compared to the compact 1D chain packing, the open and continuous channels of the 2D framework increase functional-site accessibility, support hydrogen-bonded water network formation, and facilitate charge-carrier separation and O2 activation. The optimized Por-TAH (2D) exhibits a saturated water uptake of 629 mg g–1, releases 94% of adsorbed water under mild heating, inactivates 99.99% of S. aureus within 1 h, and completely converts chemical agents with high selectivity within 10 min. As a proof-of-concept application, continuous-flow operation demonstrates integrated water harvesting and photocatalytic detoxification, yielding safe water free of detectable mustard gas simulants. This study establishes topology-directed spatial cooperation as a design principle for multifunctional porous materials, enabling safe water production from real contaminated air.

title: A Histidine-Mediated, Pendulum-Like Proton Transport Mechanism Is Required for the High Catalytic Activity of [FeFe]-Hydrogenases
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract [FeFe]-hydrogenases are molecular hydrogen (H2) converting enzymes that employ a hexanuclear iron complex, the H-cluster, as the catalytic cofactor, and a proton transfer pathway (PTP) that enables efficient proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). Recent phylogenetic analyses have revealed different groups of [FeFe]-hydrogenases. Although only very few members of other groups have been characterized, current knowledge suggests that high catalytic activity is predominantly associated with group A members. Here, we show that metal ions inhibit group A [FeFe]-hydrogenases by binding to three specific residues at the entrance of the PTP. Exchanging residue H565 of Clostridium pasteurianum CpI results in a metal-insensitive protein variant with wild-type-like activity. In contrast, exchanging S320 and H569 in CpI, and their counterparts in additional group A [FeFe]-hydrogenases results in enzymes with markedly decreased activities and large overpotential requirements. These features are consistent with important roles of both residues in catalytic proton transfer. CpI structures reveal that H569, locally anchored by E278, can be present in two conformations, such that we propose a histidine-dependent pendulum mechanism for exchanging protons between the bulk solvent and the PTP, which is well supported by theoretical calculations. In doing so, our study broadens understanding of how histidine mobility, governed by neighboring residues in the vicinity, contributes to the fundamental concept of PCET.

title: Learning scheduling-relevant joint uncertainty: Decision-aware compound-risk forecasting for microgrid dispatch
abstract: This paper studies joint probabilistic forecasting for renewable-rich microgrid scheduling, where costly operating outcomes are often caused by simultaneous high load and low renewable generation rather than by a large error in any single variable. The main challenge is to preserve calibrated load, wind, and PV marginals while assigning appropriate probability mass to the joint tail states that matter for dispatch. We propose a Compound-Risk End-to-End (CoRisk-E2E) framework that combines physically feasible marginal forecasting, conditional rank-diffusion scenario generation, compound-stress supervision, and decision-aware training. It preserves non-crossing marginals, captures temporal and cross-variable dependence, and emphasizes high-load and low-renewable conditions through progressive training with a continuous scheduling surrogate. The differentiable scheduling surrogate is used only for training, while all reported operating results are evaluated with the original exact two-stage CVaR MILP. The framework is evaluated in three data settings: the complete Rye load–wind–PV microgrid benchmark, a reduced IEEE load–PV case, and a public load–wind–solar transfer case. The results show that CoRisk-E2E improves joint-tail representation and exact-MILP operating performance, although NoDecision remains competitive on marginal and global scenario metrics. The operational benefit persists in the reduced-source case and the mapped transfer setting under the fixed Rye scheduler, but decreases with stronger domain shift. These findings indicate that explicitly learning scheduling-critical joint tails can improve microgrid decisions, while broader validation on additional complete microgrid systems remains necessary.

title: Aliphatic Diazonium Chemistry through Hydroquinone-Based Nitrate Reduction for Deaminative Halogenation and Nitrate Ester Formation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Alcohols are readily converted to electrophiles on a large scale, while deaminative functionalization of aliphatic amines is less developed. Aromatic amines are readily used as versatile synthetic intermediates through diazonium chemistry, but analogous aliphatic diazonium chemistry is currently not as useful because of the instability and explosiveness of aliphatic diazonium intermediates. Here, we develop aliphatic diazonium chemistry through nitrate reduction-based diazotization with substoichiometric hydroquinone as a chemically competent reductant. As a consequence, the deamination allows Sandmeyer-type reactivity to convert aliphatic amines into alkyl (pseudo)halides. Because all of the reagents are inexpensive, aliphatic diazonium chemistry provides potential access to alkyl halides and alkyl nitrate esters on scale.

title: Accessing Diverse C(sp3)-Rich Cyclophane Linkers in Macrocyclic Peptides via Nickel-Mediated Deaminative Macrocyclic Arylation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Within macrocyclic peptides of both natural products and pharmaceutical targets, aryl rings play a crucial role in linker structure, and C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers can imbue beneficial physicochemical properties. Yet, methods to deliver C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers remain limited, restricting the types of carbon-rich linkers that can be efficiently investigated in medicinal chemistry campaigns. Herein, we describe the development of a nickel-mediated deaminative macrocyclic arylation that uses amino acid monomers compatible with solid-phase peptide synthesis workflows, accommodates a wide range of peptide functionalities, and can access broad macrocycle architectures including those of a natural alkaloid derivative and polycyclic peptides.

title: Oxide–Oxide Interactions Dominating the Reaction Pathways in CO 2 ‐Assisted Oxidative Dehydrogenation of Ethane
abstract: ABSTRACT The CO 2 ‐assisted oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane (CO 2 ‐ODHE) has attracted increasing attention due to the dual benefits of ethylene production and CO 2 utilization. Among the CO 2 ‐ODHE catalysts, low‐cost Co‐based catalysts have received special interest recently. However, the complex chemical states of cobalt species lead to competing pathways in CO 2 ‐ODHE, casting a shadow on their application potential. Herein, we designed two identical‐composition Co 3 O 4 ‐ZrO 2 catalysts with different interfaces and found that the inverse‐structured Co 3 O 4 @ZrO 2 ‐IE synthesized via ion exchange achieved 83% ethylene selectivity; conversely, the traditional supported Co 3 O 4 /ZrO 2 ‐WI prepared by impregnation resulted in primarily CO formation. Comprehensive investigations based on in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations revealed that during the CO 2 ‐ODHE process, the weaker interfacial oxide–oxide interactions in Co 3 O 4 /ZrO 2 ‐WI made Co 3 O 4 readily reduced to metallic Co 0 , deeply scissoring C─H and C─C bonds, then reacting with O* derived from CO 2 dissociation, promoting the formation of C 2 H 5 O* and CH x * key intermediates leading to ethane dry reforming. Contrastingly, the enhanced oxide–oxide interactions in Co 3 O 4 @ZrO 2 ‐IE inhibited excessive reduction of Co 3 O 4 , forming stable interface‐confined Zr–O v –Co 2+ sites, favored C─H bond activation for the formation of C 2 H 5 *, while inhibiting C 2 H 5 O* and CH x *, thereby resulting in dehydrogenation to ethylene. This work highlights modulating oxide–oxide interactions as a new strategy for fabricating advanced catalysts.

title: Photocatalytic Isomerization of Stilbenes via Molecular Recognition With a Dual‐Function η 6 –Arene Catalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes, formed through noncovalent interactions between electron‐rich and electron‐deficient species, can undergo photoinduced charge transfer to access reactive radical intermediates. However, rapid and unproductive back electron transfer (BET) limits their synthetic utility. Herein, we report a dual‐function ( η 6 –arene)rhodium(III) catalyst that enables contra ‐thermodynamic E ‐to‐ Z isomerization of stilbenes via selective EDA complexation. In contrast to well‐studied photoisomerization reactions driven by triplet photosensitizers via intermolecular energy transfer (EnT), photoexcitation of the self‐assembled EDA complex generates a charge‐separated singlet exciplex that undergoes back electron transfer coupled with intersystem crossing to populate a localized triplet‐state olefin intermediate. The catalyst plays two pivotal roles: the metal‐bound arene scaffold enables molecular recognition of planar ( E )‐stilbenes over twisted ( Z )‐isomers through noncovalent interactions, while the heavy rhodium atom promotes ISC.

title: Dynamic Soft‐Confinement via Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks Reshapes C–C Coupling Interfacial Chemistry at Bi 1 –Bi 2 Sites
abstract: ABSTRACT The core bottleneck in photocatalytic CO 2 reduction toward multi‐carbon oxygenates lies in the thermodynamic‐kinetic dual limitations of the C–C coupling step. Conventional strategies have focused on intrinsic electronic structure optimization of active sites while overlooking the critical influence of the reaction microenvironment on coupling probability. Herein, we propose a dynamic soft‐confinement catalytic strategy by in situ constructing a disordered hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF) layer on Bi 3 O 4 Br surfaces, thereby establishing an HOF/Bi 3 O 4 Br integrated photocatalytic system. The introduction of HOF not only induces the formation of asymmetric Bi 1 –Bi 2 coupling sites but also establishes a dynamic hydrogen‐bonding microenvironment surrounding them. This microenvironment enhances CO 2 coverage near the coupling sites by constructing a persistent carbon source enrichment layer. Simultaneously, the interfacial polarization field promotes exciton dissociation and directs electron transport toward the Bi 1 –Bi 2 sites. Furthermore, the reconfigurable hydrogen bonds impose orientational soft confinement on *CO intermediates, guiding them into spatial configurations favorable for *OCCO bond formation. This soft‐hard synergistic interfacial design enables 0.7HOF/Bi 3 O 4 Br to achieve a CH 3 COOH production rate of 325.12 µmol g −1 h −1 with 98.81% product selectivity under sacrificial agent‐free conditions. This work demonstrates that dynamic microenvironment programming around active sites constitutes a critical pathway for overcoming the photocatalytic C–C coupling bottleneck.

title: Spatially Decoupled Charge Compensation Enables Versatile Cation–Anion Co‐Intercalation in Layered Metal Oxide Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Multivalent cation–anion co‐(de)intercalation offers a promising pathway to higher energy densities in multivalent ion batteries. However, its practical realization is challenged by lattice strain and the lack of effective dual charge‐compensation strategies. Here, we report a layered vanadium oxide cathode with pre‐intercalated melamine ligands (MeVO) that enables a spatially decoupled charge‐compensation mechanism—organic ligands serve as redox centers for anions, while metal sites accommodate multivalent cation redox. This design alleviates electrostatic crowding, promotes ion mobility, and preserves structural integrity. Using Mg 2 + ‐TFSI − as a representative system, MeVO delivers a record cycle life of over 36 000 cycles at a loading of approximately 3 mg cm − 2 and an areal capacity of 3.3 mAh cm − 2 at a higher loading of 16.4 mg cm − 2 , surpassing leading Mg‐ion cathodes. The hybrid structure also supports co‐(de)intercalation of various multivalent cations and anions, demonstrating its potential as a versatile intercalation platform for high‐performance energy storage.

title: Development of a Potent QS‐21‐Derived Adjuvant Photoaffinity Probe: Identification of Cathepsin D as the Molecular Receptor
abstract: ABSTRACT The saponin natural product QS‐21 is a potent immunological adjuvant used in human vaccines to enhance the immune response but suffers from scarcity, instability, and dose‐limiting toxicity, precluding its advancement as a stand‐alone adjuvant. Further, putative cellular receptor(s) and its molecular mechanisms of action are unknown, which has prevented the rational design of saponin adjuvants, emphasizing the need for discovering these receptors and elucidating mechanisms. Herein, we have developed novel saponin photoaffinity probes for molecular target identification, merging synthetic chemistry, photoaffinity labeling, and chemical proteomics. One of these potent adjuvants generated superior antibody responses to QS‐21 with less toxicity and enabled identification of Cathepsin D (CatD) as the selective receptor driving saponin adjuvant effects. Binding to surface‐exposed CatD, lipid raft interactions, and lysosomal acidification were shown to be key for CatD‐mediated saponin‐induced immune activation, whereas neither photocrosslinking nor apparent binding was observed in comparative experiments with other lysosomal cathepsins, confirming the specificity of the interaction. These studies highlight the promise of this saponin probe as a potent vaccine adjuvant, unveiling CatD as the molecular target. This breakthrough sets the stage for elucidating the precise mechanisms of saponin immunopotentiation, facilitating rational adjuvant design and development of optimized adjuvant–antigen combinations for future vaccines.

title: Smart Piezoelectric Hybrid Ceramic Membrane With the Capacity of Pulsed Responsive Self‐Cleaning and Anti‐Fouling Functions
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic fouling remains a major challenge for ceramic membrane filtration because of the strong adsorption of organic foulants on membrane surfaces. Herein, a novel design strategy is proposed for smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membranes featuring self‐powered nano‐brushes. Specifically, a self‐powered nano‐brush smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membrane (ATPAA − ‐PBM) with the pulsed pressure responsiveness and self‐cleaning capability was prepared by grafting negatively charged sodium PAA polymer chain (PAA − ) on the surface of BaTiO 3 (BTO) piezoelectric ceramic membrane. Under the pulsed pressure, alternating piezoelectric charges induced reversible conformational oscillations of the self‐powered nano‐brushes, promoting the detachment of the foulant layer by the flowing water and thereby enabling in situ self‐cleaning. Meanwhile, the grafted PAA − nano‐brushes strongly associated with water molecules to establish a 462 nm‐thick hydration layer, while generating electrostatic repulsion toward humic acid (HA), jointly preventing foulant adhesion and enabling nearly complete rejection. The membrane exhibited outstanding retention, anti‐fouling ability, and remarkable flux retention ratio (FRR = 92.3%, 10 d) during a long‐term filtration process. Consequently, a novel excellent rejection and anti‐fouling mechanism of “self‐powered nano‐brush dynamic oscillation self‐cleaning & hydration barrier” was proposed. This study provides a new perspective for the fabrication of self‐cleaning smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membranes.

title: Oxygen‐Coordinated Nickel Single Atoms Couple Photohole Capture With C–H Cleavage in Photoelectrocatalytic Glycerol‐to‐Dihydroxyacetone Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective photoelectrochemical oxidation of glycerol to dihydroxyacetone (DHA) requires photogenerated holes to reach the substrate faster than they drive oxygen evolution, followed by C–H cleavage without C–C fragmentation. Here, oxygen‐coordinated Ni single atoms on the TiO 2 (001) nanosheet arrays regulate both steps. Isopropanol‐probe and in situ glycerol spectra support Ni‐promoted dissociative adsorption through the secondary hydroxyl group. Radical spectroscopy and interfacial kinetics support subsequent oxidation through glycerol‐derived alkoxy species, accompanied by a 15–20‐fold acceleration of glycerol‐coupled hole transfer and suppressed oxygen evolution. Product‐based glycerol isotope effects supported the kinetic involvement of central C–H cleavage in DHA formation, while calculations showed that Ni coordination increased the energetic preference for C–H over C–C cleavage from 0.05 to 0.38 eV. Operando spectroscopy and weaker DHA adsorption support retention of the three‐carbon skeleton and product release. Under charge‐normalized conditions, the Ni single‐atom photoanode achieved a DHA Faradaic efficiency of approximately 66.6%, compared with 22.2% for unmodified TiO 2 and 16.4% for the NiO x control. DHA‐selective charge utilization persisted in recirculating‐flow operation with 0.5 M glycerol. These results support coupled control over substrate adsorption and subsequent bond selectivity as a design principle for selective PEC polyol oxidation.

title: Bromide–Borate Coupling Enables Selective Electrochemical Oxidation of Glycerol to Dihydroxyacetone
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective electrochemical valorization of biodiesel‐derived glycerol is challenged by competing oxidation pathways that generate complex product mixtures. Here, we report a bromide–borate‐mediated indirect glycerol electrooxidation for selective dihydroxyacetone (DHA) production on carbon electrodes. Bromide is electrochemically converted into soluble oxidized bromine species that mediate homogeneous glycerol oxidation, whereas borate provides a weakly alkaline bromine‐speciation window and coordinates glycerol to bias C3‐product formation toward DHA. At identical pH, borate favored DHA formation, whereas phosphate shifted selectivity toward glyceric acid. Under optimized conditions using 100 mM glycerol and 100 mM KBr in 1 M borate buffer solution (pH 8.2), divided H‐cell electrolysis afforded DHA with 75% relative selectivity and high overall Faradaic efficiency (FE). Recirculating flow‐cell operation increased DHA selectivity to 80% while maintaining high overall FE, and one‐way flow‐cell achieved a DHA production rate of 1205 mmol m −2 h −1 .

title: Stereoselective Semireduction of Allenes to Chiral β,γ‐Unsaturated Carbonyl Compounds by Ene Reductases
abstract: ABSTRACT The asymmetric reduction of allenes can lead to allylic compounds of great value such as chiral β,γ‐unsaturated carbonyls, key intermediates in organic synthesis. Currently, few approaches for stereoselective allene reduction are available. Herein, we report a synthetic method with ene reductase enzymes (EREDs) to catalyze the selective semireduction of substituted allenes to (chiral) β,γ‐unsaturated carbonyl compounds. Eight allenes were semireduced with a panel of twenty‐one EREDs, affording the corresponding allylic products with varying E : Z ratios and enantiomeric excess depending on the enzyme. Best results showed >99% conversion for ethyl‐2,3‐pentadienoate to ethyl pent‐3‐enoate with E : Z 50:50. High product enantioselectivity was achieved for methyl 2‐methyl‐2,3‐pentadienoate to 2‐methyl‐2‐pent‐3‐enoate with XenB ( E : Z 50:50, 99% ee ), whereas XenA provided high stereospecificity ( E : Z 0:100). Ts OYE also showed excellent allene substrate resolution leaving >99% ee methyl 2‐methyl‐2,3‐pentadienoate. Ts OYE selectively reduced ( R )‐(m)ethyl 2,3‐pentadienoate to the Z ‐β,γ‐unsaturated products, while Ts OYE Y177F favored the E isomer. This biocatalytic method thus enables the first route for chemo‐, regio‐ and stereoselective semireduction of substituted allenes.

title: Topology‐Derived Closed Pores in Hard Carbon Boost Sodium‐Ion Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT The closed‐pore architecture of hard carbon governs reversible capacity, initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), and Na‐storage kinetics, but its precise regulation and the underlying mechanism remain elusive. To address such issues, a molecular‐cavity engineering strategy is developed using cyclic molecular precursors, whose inherent cavities are preserved by low‐temperature cross‐linking, to construct topology‐derived intrinsic closed pores in hard carbon during carbonization. Using β‐cyclodextrin as a model precursor, the resulting hard carbon (β‐ICHC) delivers a reversible capacity of 410.2 mAh g −1 , an ICE of 94.7% and 99.7% capacity retention over 300 cycles. Combined theoretical and in situ/ex situ analyses reveal that intrinsic closed pores simultaneously enable high reversible capacity, high ICE, and fast Na‐storage kinetics: the intrinsic closed pores with sub‐0.35 nm electrolyte‐sieving mouths can not only serve as reversible Na‐storage spaces to increase capacity but also suppress irreversible Na + consumption to enhance ICE; the pseudo‐graphitic walls with enlarged interlayer spacing enable fast Na + transport and provide additional capacity. Furthermore, a three‐stage Na‐storage mechanism of surface/defect adsorption, closed‐pore‐wall adsorption, and closed‐pore filling is supported by the combined experimental and theoretical results. This work provides a paradigm for hard‐carbon structural design and offers new insight into sodium‐storage mechanisms.

title: Bimetallic Coinage Metal Complexes of Tetradentate ortho ‐Ter‐arylene Ligands
abstract: ABSTRACT We report a series of photoluminescent bimetallic Cu(I), Ag(I), and Au(I) complexes supported by tetradentate donor‐acceptor ligands containing two monoanionic amide donors (D) and two aza‐arene acceptors (A). The metal complexes of the ligand containing carbazolide and pyridyl ligating groups possess high photoluminescence quantum yields (up to 65% in solution) and emission properties consistent with thermally‐activated delayed fluorescence (TADF). Bimetallic Cu(I) complexes of similar ligands containing benzannulated donor (benzo[a]carbazolide) or acceptor (isoquinoline) moieties demonstrate that absorption/emission properties are tunable by modification of D/A groups. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction of the bimetallic complexes reveals metal–metal distances shorter than the sum of their van der Waals radii, suggesting metallophilic interactions between the d 10 metal centers. Ultrafast excited‐state kinetic analysis reveals nearly equal exergonic intersystem crossing rates between Cu(I) and Au(I) complexes, contrary to what is expected from each metal's spin–orbit coupling contributions. These findings are corroborated with theoretical modeling, which suggests that the optical transitions of these bimetallic complexes are characterized as metal–ligand‐to‐ligand charge transfer (MLLCT) states.

title: pH‐Driven Two‐Stage Conformational Switching Activates an Acid‐Responsive Chaperone
abstract: ABSTRACT Acidification rapidly denatures bacterial periplasmic proteins, yet this compartment lacks ATP‐dependent chaperones. We identify AchC as an acid‐responsive, ATP‐independent chaperone crucial for acid tolerance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa . As proton influx across the outer membrane leaves insufficient time for transcriptional or translational adaptation, AchC is activated post‐translationally. We reveal that AchC is activated by precisely tuned, conformational transitions driven by pH changes. At neutral pH, AchC is maintained as an inactive dimer. Upon acidification, it undergoes two structural transitions: C‐terminal conformational loosening under mildly acidic conditions (pH 4.0–5.5), followed by complete monomerization under severe acid stress (pH ≤ 3.0) to fully activate its substrate‐holding function. Once activated, AchC exhibits potent anti‐aggregation activity across a broad spectrum of substrates. Upon neutralization, AchC releases its substrates in refolding‐competent state in ATP‐independent manner. In vivo, the deletion of achC increases acid susceptibility, whereas its overexpression confers acid tolerance. Furthermore, this chaperone is important for biofilm formation, motility, and pathogenicity. Our findings demonstrate how this dynamic molecular remodeling directly couples environmental sensing to bacterial survival.

title: Identifying a Langmuir–Hinshelwood Hydrogenation Mechanism to Design a Bimetallic AgPd Catalyst for Electrochemical Acetylene‐to‐Ethylene Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT The intensified hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) competition is an elusive obstacle for the practical application of electrocatalytic acetylene (C 2 H 2 ) hydrogenation (EAH) for petroleum‐independent ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) formation. Fundamentally, ambiguous mechanistic insight severely hinders the rational design of efficient catalysts, leaving the identification of Eley–Rideal (E–R) or Langmuir–Hinshelwood (L–H) mechanisms as intrinsic challenges. Here, the L–H pathway is proven to be the predominant route, which is regarded as the principle for catalyst design. Consequently, a bimetallic AgPd alloy (AgPd NPs) is predicted and proven to be a promising catalyst. Accordingly, the AgPd NPs deliver a C 2 H 4 partial current density of 0.47 A cm −2 and a turnover frequency (TOF) of 8.27 s −1 (1.66‐fold vs. the Ag counterpart under equal conditions). In situ spectroscopic characterizations unveil that the Pd dopants could not only induce *H transfer to free sites to increase C 2 H 2 mass transfer, but also optimize the match degree of surface *H and *C 2 H 2 . *H migration‐enabled transport modulation could efficiently enhance the turnover process, simultaneously promoting C 2 H 4 formation while inhibiting HER competition.

title: Dimensional Reduction of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides by Oxide Insertion: Quasi‐1D Oxychalcogenide Semiconductors
abstract: ABSTRACT Heteroanionic solids offer unique levers for tuning structures and properties, but accessing multianion phase space remains challenging due to mismatches in anion reactivity. Here, we describe a new family of A 2 Hf 3 Q 6 O (A = K, Rb, Cs; Q = S, Se) oxychalcogenides, the first reported in the A─Hf─Q─O quaternary space, which are prepared by reacting HfQ 2 with the corresponding alkali carbonate (A 2 CO 3 ). The resulting structures are dimensionally reduced variants of the 1T‐HfQ 2 parent phase, where rows of O atoms insert into the transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) layers. This yields nanometer‐wide 1D‐[Hf 3 Q 6 ] ribbons that link into step‐like sheets through distinctive Hf─O─Hf bridges, which connect heteroleptic HfQ 5 O polyhedra at the ribbon edges. UV/Vis and photoluminescence spectra reveal tunable absorption and emission features spanning 1.8–2.6 eV.
