Calculated band structures show direct‐gap transitions and highly dispersive bands along the [Hf 3 Q 6 ] nanoribbons, yielding effective masses more than two orders of magnitude lower than in other crystallographic directions. Charge‐density plots further illustrate quasi‐1D electronic anisotropy, showing frontier orbitals confined to the nanoribbons due to covalent Hf─Q bonding. We anticipate heteroanion‐driven dimensional reduction can be used to engineer anisotropy in semiconductors and offers new routes to synthetically challenging multianion systems.

title: Sequence‐Controlled Helical Ladder Polymers: Impact of Stereochemical Sequence on Helical Geometry and Chiral Recognition
abstract: ABSTRACT Amylose and cellulose possess diastereomeric repeating units and adopt distinct left‐handed 6/1‐ and sheet‐shaped 2/1‐helical structures, respectively, while their chemically‐modified derivatives display complementary chiral recognition abilities due to their inherent homochiral diastereomeric repeating units with different secondary structures. We now report a modular synthetic strategy for constructing helical ladder polymers with different sequences in which the stereochemical combination of two chiral ladder motifs dictates the helical geometry and chiral recognition function. Alternating annulation of the ( S )‐ or ( R )‐1,1′‐spirobiindane units with ( S )‐ or ( R )‐2,2′‐tethered 1,1′‐binaphthyl units afforded coil‐ and ribbon‐type diastereomeric helices along with their enantiomeric counterparts. These coil‐ and ribbon‐type diastereomeric helical ladders showed complementary chiral recognition when used as chiral stationary phases for liquid chromatography, whereas the corresponding nonhelical precursors exhibited no resolution capability. The corresponding enantiomeric helices showed reversal of the enantiomer elution order while retaining a comparable enantioseparation ability. These results establish modularly designed sequence‐controlled helical ladders as chiral platforms with programmable secondary structures and chiral functions.

title: Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are fungal pathogens that cause life-threatening infections, including cryptococcal meningitis. A distinctive feature of the cryptococcal cell wall is the extensive deacetylation of chitin to chitosan, a modification that is essential for virulence but whose structural role in cell-wall organization remains poorly understood. Here, we analyze the cell walls of wild-type strains of both species and their avirulent chitosan-deficient mutants, which serve as vaccine candidates. Loss of chitosan disrupted cell morphology and altered cell-wall ultrastructure, with more pronounced defects in C. neoformans. Solid-state NMR reveals that aggregated α-(1→3)-glucans form the principal rigid domain of the cell wall in both species and are closely associated with chitin microfibrils, whereas surrounding β-glucans and mannoproteins constitute a more dynamic matrix. Chitosan modulates hydration and flexibility, and its loss increases chitin exposure and triggers species-specific remodeling of the polysaccharide network. In C. neoformans, chitosan depletion increased α-(1→3)-glucan content and reduced β-glucan levels, whereas C. gattii selectively lost one α-(1→3)-glucan subtype while maintaining β-glucan levels. Although capsule production remained intact, chitosan deficiency altered glucuronoxylomannan linkage patterns and mannoprotein composition. These findings reveal how chitosan organizes cryptococcal cell-wall architecture and highlight distinct structural adaptation strategies among pathogenic Cryptococcus species.

title: Disentangling Polaron Formation Pathways in Y6 by Probing Noninteracting and Interacting Chromophores via Transient Absorption Spectroscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT In highly efficient organic solar cells, the optoelectronic properties of the non‐fullerene acceptor Y6 are governed by the molecular packing of noninteracting and interacting molecules. In this study, steady‐state and transient absorption spectroscopy are employed to disentangle the spectral signatures and excited‐state dynamics of interacting and noninteracting Y6 in solution and thin films. By controlling aggregation in dilute solution, we identify localized Frenkel‐type excitons (LE) on noninteracting Y6 and aggregate excitons (AE) on intermolecular interacting Y6. The AEs exhibit strongly fluence‐dependent lifetimes (30–200 ps) governed by singlet–singlet annihilation, whereas localized excitons decay monoexponentially on a nanosecond timescale. Furthermore, long‐lived polaronic states are observed to form on aggregated Y6 within tens of picoseconds and persist into the nanosecond regime. Comparison with thin‐film measurements reveals similar processes with an additional ultrafast energy transfer from noninteracting chromophores to aggregated domains. These results establish a consistent framework for assigning transient absorption features in Y6 and suggest that, in neat films of Y6, the pairwise formation of polarons arises from an Onsager‐like autoionization process of delocalized excitons in domains of interacting Y6 with moderate yield. This provides central insight into charge‐generation mechanisms in Y6‐based photovoltaic systems.

title: Chiral Phonon–Driven Ultrafast Spin Currents in a Non‐Magnetic Ferroelectric
abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery that fundamental lattice vibrations can carry angular momentum allows non‐magnetic materials to exhibit properties that until now have only been observable in magnetic materials. However, the role of these specific vibrations, commonly known as chiral phonons, in driving ultrafast spin dynamics has not yet been explored experimentally. Here, using broadband terahertz emission spectroscopy, we demonstrate that the non‐magnetic ferroelectric generates signals consistent with a ultrafast spin current after excitation with an ultrafast laser pulse, which we attribute to a chiral phonon–induced spin Seebeck effect. We suggest that the transient heating creates an non‐equilibrium phonon distribution, resulting in a net angular momentum and magnetization perpendicular to the thermal gradient, which is converted into a terahertz electromagnetic pulse via an inverse spin‐Hall effect in a thin metal overlayer. The emitted field reverses sign upon flipping the sample orientation or replacing Pt with W, consistent with spin‐current generation. Polarization‐resolved measurements reveal controllable terahertz ellipticity, indicating an additional polarization‐dependent ultrafast response. Our results establish chiral phonons as a route for generating ultrafast spin currents in non‐magnetic materials as well as providing a pathway toward terahertz sources with switchable handedness.

title: Stress‐Resistant Plant Cell‐Wall Inspired Cell Armor Enables Red Blood Cell Lyophilization
abstract: ABSTRACT Lyophilization offers an attractive route for ambient‐temperature storage of biological systems by eliminating cold‐chain dependence and suppressing solution‐phase degradation. However, lyophilizing mammalian cells remains challenging due to their vulnerability to coupled stresses, including ice‐induced mechanical injury and membrane destabilization during freezing and dehydration. In nature, stress‐resistant plant cells survive extreme conditions through multifunctional cell walls. Inspired by their natural survival strategies, we engineer an artificial membrane armor (AMA) that enables efficient lyophilization of red blood cells (RBCs). This biomimetic AMA integrates a nanoporous zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF‐8) for mechanical support, a water‐retentive polymer matrix for hydration retention and colloidal stabilization, and Zn 2 + coordination preserves membrane fluidity and suppresses freeze‐ and dehydration‐driven membrane phase transitions. Through synergistic interfacial protection, the AMA effectively buffers coupled stresses associated with lyophilization, enabling ∼95% post‐rehydration recovery of RBCs using an ultra‐low protectant content (

title: Emerging Lipid Nanoparticle Targeting Strategies for Extrahepatic Delivery of RNA Therapeutics
abstract: ABSTRACT Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed RNA therapeutics through their high delivery efficiency, scalable manufacturing, and favorable safety profiles, as demonstrated by COVID‐19 mRNA vaccines and clinically approved small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics. However, extending RNA delivery beyond the liver to extrahepatic tissues, including the spleen, lungs, lymph nodes, brain, and tumors, remains challenging because of the intrinsic hepatotropism of conventional LNPs and their limited cell‐type specificity. Recent advances in lipid chemistry, particle engineering, surface functionalization, protein corona modulation, and route‐specific administration have enabled new strategies to redirect LNPs toward specific tissues and cell populations. This review systematically examines these approaches and highlights key determinants of LNP tropism, including formulation composition, surface properties, endogenous protein adsorption, and administration route. We further discuss the clinical translation of extrahepatic LNP delivery, covering clinically validated products, emerging therapeutic candidates, and gaps between preclinical models and human applications. Major challenges include cell‐resolved biodistribution, long‐term safety, repeated‐dose immunogenicity, cross‐study comparability, and standardized quantitative assessment. Finally, we explore how high‐throughput screening, machine learning, and data‐driven design can accelerate the rational optimization of next‐generation LNPs. These advances may facilitate precise tissue‐ and cell‐selective RNA delivery, expanding the therapeutic potential of RNA medicines beyond the liver.

title: A Simple Descriptor for Solid‐State Ionic Conductors Across Chemistries
abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery of new solid‐state ionic conductors remains challenging because ion transport depends sensitively on both mobile‐ion chemistry and the host crystal framework. Although atomistic calculations can evaluate migration barriers directly, simple descriptors can greatly facilitate screening large materials spaces and gaining mechanistic insight. However, existing descriptors often show limited transferability across mobile‐ion chemistries and material classes. Here, we generate a diverse dataset of ion‐migration barriers spanning Li‐, Na‐, K‐, and Mg‐ion conductors across oxides, sulfides, and halides, and use it to systematically benchmark descriptors. From this analysis, we devise distance contraction, ∆ d , a simple local geometric descriptor that measures the largest contraction of mobile‐ion–neighbor distances relative to their equilibrium values along a migration pathway. This quantity captures the dominant short‐range repulsion penalty associated with ion migration and consistently distinguishes low‐ from high‐barrier pathways across chemistries. Using ∆ d in a high‐throughput screening workflow, we recover many known fast‐ion conductors and identify previously unexplored candidates, with fast‐ion transport validated by nudged elastic band calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. Beyond screening, ∆ d links diverse ion‐transport mechanisms to a common physical quantity: The largest distance contraction experienced by the migrating ion.

title: Robust Dipicolinic Acid‐Anchored Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Wide‐Bandgap and Tandem Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT The anchoring group of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) hole‐transporting materials dictates both substrate binding and interfacial passivation, serving as a key lever for high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics. Herein, we report a novel SAM molecular material, denoted by XS21 , engineered with a multidentate dipicolinic acid (DPA) anchoring core to address conventional adhesion and degradation limitations. From an experimental perspective, the DPA anchor is found to promote molecular chemisorption onto the substrate, potentially originating from the dual‐action mechanism of pyridine–Ni coordination coupled with dicarboxylate‐metal interaction. Furthermore, XS21 imparts both low acid‐dissociation constants ( K a ) and superior ultraviolet (UV) photostability. Consequently, wide‐bandgap (1.79 eV) perovskite solar cells containing XS21 deliver a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.54% with an exceptional open‐circuit voltage of 1.372 V. Crucially, integrating XS21 into monolithic all‐perovskite tandem solar cells yields a remarkable PCE of 29.62%, alongside an outstanding operational stability (retaining >90% of initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation). This work establishes multi‐dentate pyridine‐carboxylate anchoring as a vital paradigm for next‐generation efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Biomimetic Dichalcogenide‐Hybrid Nanozymes With Glutathione Peroxidase‐Like Activity for Liver Protection
abstract: ABSTRACT Glutathione peroxidase (GPX)‐mimetic nanozymes are a promising strategy to restore redox homeostasis, but many existing systems rely on metals and remain limited by cytotoxicity, poor selectivity, and susceptibility to catalytic deactivation. Inspired by the active‐site chemistry of native GPX, we designed dichalcogenide‐hybrid mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as inorganic–organic nanozymes with tunable sulfur and selenium environments. Structure–activity analysis showed that GPX‐like performance is governed by chalcogen composition, chalcogen density, and spatial proximity of S/Se within the framework, which together regulate reversible disulfide/diselenide redox cycling and substrate access. Among the materials tested, the diselenide–hybrid framework exhibited the highest activity, with improved selectivity and biocompatibility relative to the disulfide‐hybrid analogue, and conventional metal‐based GPX mimics. Mechanistic studies indicated efficient glutathione‐dependent detoxification of peroxides and lipid peroxides through catalytically active chalcogen intermediates. In vivo, the optimized diselenide‐hybrid material protected against acetaminophen‐induced and rifampicin‐induced liver injury, reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, restored antioxidant capacity, and improved survival. It also alleviated steatosis and metabolic dysfunction in metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) models. These findings establish dichalcogenide–hybrid frameworks as effective GPX‐like nanozymes and a promising platform for the treatment of oxidative stress‐associated liver diseases.

title: Engineering Advanced Electrocatalysts for Energy‐Saving Zinc−Air Hybrid Batteries: Concurrent Energy Storage Coupled With Chemical Upgrading
abstract: ABSTRACT Additive‐assisted zinc−air hybrid batteries (ZAHBs) that couple favorable additive oxidation with oxygen reduction represent ideal energy storage candidates, distinguished by high theoretical energy density, reduced charging voltage, and functionality for electrochemical upgrading of organics or wastewater. Herein, a critical overview of ZAHBs is provided, commencing with the fundamental electrochemistry (including advantages, working mechanisms, cell configurations, and evaluation parameters) and the selection criteria for small‐molecule additives (including theoretical potential, solubility, stability, toxicity, and volatility). We then summarize recent progress in three categories of ZAHBs (i.e., wastewater‐purified, value‐added, and redox‐mediated), discussing alternative anodic oxidation reactions (e.g., alcohol, urea, hydrazine, and iodine oxidation) coupled with cathodic oxygen reduction, along with the underlying catalytic mechanisms. Particular emphasis is placed on catalyst design strategies spanning electronic (ligand engineering, heteroatom doping, electron delocalization, orbital hybridization, and built‐in electric field), geometric (defect engineering, curvature engineering, and nano‐confinement effect), and interfacial (high‐energy interface, heterostructure, interfacial microenvironment, and core–shell structure) modulations. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges and future perspectives for advancing ZAHBs. This review offers valuable guidance for the rational design and practical deployment of next‐generation energy devices.

title: Robust Spin Splitting and Fermiology in the Layered Altermagnet CoNb4Se8
abstract: ABSTRACT Altermagnetism defies conventional classifications of collinear magnetic phases, combining compensated magnetization with momentum‐dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting. While altermagnetic band splitting has been established in three‐dimensional compounds such as MnTe and CrSb, layered altermagnets remain far less explored spectroscopically. Here, combining termination‐resolved micro‐ARPES, fine photon‐energy mapping, spin‐ARPES, and density functional theory, we map the three‐dimensional fermiology of the layered g ‐wave altermagnet , obtained by ordered Co intercalation of 2H‐. We resolve the spin–split branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw photoemission spectra and, with spin‐ARPES at these experimentally identified momenta, show the reversal of the spin polarization at opposite momenta and between two regions of the sample, consistent with opposite time‐reversal domains, and its absence along the symmetry‐protected nodal –K direction. We further report a weak low‐temperature anomaly near T 0 ≈ 50–60 K, detected by magnetometry, temperature‐dependent micro‐ARPES, and ultrafast reflectivity, whose microscopic origin remains open. These results provide a momentum‐resolved benchmark of the electronic structure of a layered altermagnet.

title: Covalently Locked Donor–Acceptor Block Copolymer Nanoparticles Enable Efficient, Stable and Reproducible Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic photocatalysts with tailored properties and unique processability offer a sustainable route to solar hydrogen. To maximize light harvesting and charge generation, donor and acceptor materials are usually physically mixed to form D:A heterojunction nanoparticles (NPs). However, weakly constrained interactions can promote phase segregation, morphological evolution, and limited reproducibility. Here, we introduce an all‐conjugated donor–acceptor block copolymer, PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT, in which covalent linkage between PBDB‐T and PYT segments constrains nanoscale donor–acceptor organization and promotes intramolecular charge transfer. Compared with nanoparticles prepared from a physical PBDB‐T:PYT blend, PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT nanoparticles exhibit stronger photoluminescence quenching, more persistent charge‐associated transient absorption features, and improved photoelectrochemical charge extraction. As a result, hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) rates exceeding 120 mmol cm −2 g −1 h −1 (>450 µmol h −1 ) are achieved with low Pt loading (b ‐PYT NPs retained 95% of the initial HER rate after 96 h of photocatalysis. Conversely, NPs prepared from physically mixed PBDB‐T and PYT show lower activity and faster deactivation, consistent with morphology‐driven losses. PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT also maintains high performance across polymer batches, improving reproducibility. These results establish all‐conjugated donor–acceptor block copolymers as a promising design strategy for combining high activity, operational stability, and reproducibility in organic nanoparticle photocatalysis.

title: Synergy Between Controllable Sulfur Defect and NiS Cocatalyst Enabling Efficient Photoredox Coupling Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Semiconductor‐based photoredox coupling of selective oxidation of vanillyl alcohol (VOL) to vanillin (VAL) with H 2 evolution provides a sustainable alternative to conventional industrial VAL synthesis processes, yet its performance is often hindered by rapid charge recombination and insufficient active sites. Herein, we report a facile one‐pot hydrothermal strategy to construct NiS‐decorated Zn 3 In 2 S 6 (ZIS) nanoflowers with controllable sulfur vacancies (V S ) for efficient co‐production of VAL and H 2 . Moderate concentrations of V S regulate the surface electronic structure and act as oxidation active sites to optimize VOL adsorption. Meanwhile, uniformly dispersed NiS cocatalysts serve as efficient electron relays and reduction active sites, accelerating charge migration and promoting H 2 generation. Benefiting from the interfacial synergy between V S and NiS, the optimal 1%NiS‐ZIS‐V S2 catalyst delivers an 18‐fold enhancement in both VAL and H 2 production rates relative to pristine ZIS, together with excellent stability and broad substrate versatility. This work highlights the critical role of defect‐cocatalyst synergy in designing advanced cooperative photoredox catalysts for sustainable chemical synthesis.

title: Ligand Electronics and Metal‐Site Acidity Enable High‐Voltage MOF Electrolytes for Quasi‐Solid‐State Lithium‐Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐metal batteries (LMBs) coupled with Ni‐rich cathodes offer high energy density for next‐generation energy storage. Their practical implementation, however, is limited by electrolyte oxidation and interfacial degradation under high voltage. Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) would regulate ion solvation and stabilize electrode‐electrolyte interfaces in quasi‐solid‐state electrolytes, yet the molecular origins of their oxidation stability remain unclear. Here, we identify ligand electronics and metal‐site acidity as key descriptors for high‐voltage‐stable MOF electrolytes. Electron‐withdrawing ligands lower the HOMO energy levels of MOFs, while hard Lewis‐acidic Al sites further enhance oxidation resistance. Guided by this principle, we design a perfluorinated Al‐based MOF, Al‐FBDC, featuring a high oxidation onset potential of 4.82 V (vs. Li + /Li). Incorporating Al‐FBDC into a composite cathode reconstructs the local electrolyte environment at particle‐level interfaces, thereby suppressing parasitic reactions and cathode degradation under high‐voltage operation. As a result, Li||Al‐FBDC@NCM quasi‐solid‐state cells deliver excellent long‐term cycling stability and rate performance, retaining 82% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C over 3.0‐4.5 V, while maintaining robust performance even at 4.6 and 4.8 V cut‐off voltages and with controlled electrolyte loading. This work identifies a general design principle for high‐voltage‐stable MOF electrolytes and offers a practical route toward high‐energy‐density LMBs.

title: Bacteroides–Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Commensal gut bacteria are key contributors to the resilience against pathogen invasion. This is exemplified by the success of faecal microbiota transplantation in treating recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection. Yet, characteristics of communities that can confer colonisation resistance and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. Here we use a synthetic community of 14 commensal gut bacteria to uncover inter-species interactions and metabolic pathways underpinning the emergent resilience against C. difficile invasion. We challenged this synthetic community as well as faecal-matter-derived communities with antibiotic treatment and C. difficile in a continuous flow bioreactor. Using generalised Lotka-Volterra and genome-scale metabolic modelling, we identified interactions between Escherichia coli and Bacteroides/Phocaeicola sp. as key to the pathogen’s suppression. Metabolomics and targeted validation experiments revealed that fructan-derived fructooligosaccharides, vitamin B3 biosynthesis, and competition for Stickland metabolism precursors causally contribute to suppression across multiple C. difficile strains and donor backgrounds. Analysis of metagenomics data from patient cohorts and clinical trials attested the in vivo relevance of the identified metabolic pathways and the ratio between Bacteroides and Escherichia in successful colonisation resistance. The latter was found to be a stronger discriminator than commonly used alpha diversity metrics. Together, our study uncovers emergent microbial interactions in pathogen resistance with implications for rational design of bacteriotherapies.

title: Site‐Selectively Engineered MoS 2 /ReS 2 Heterostructures for High‐Performance Supercapacitors
abstract: ABSTRACT Layered MoS 2 holds great potential for supercapacitors; however, its intrinsically low electrical conductivity, sluggish electrochemical kinetics, and susceptibility to Mo dissolution severely hamper its electrochemical performance. Here, we propose a selective‐doping‐coupled heterostructure engineering strategy, in which atomic Fe preferentially incorporates into the MoS 2 domain, while the local structure of the ReS 2 component remains largely preserved, forming an Fe‐doped MoS 2 /ReS 2 (Fe‐MRS) heterostructure. Theoretical and experimental results reveal the formation of a built‐in electric field at the Fe‐MRS interface, driving electron transfer from ReS 2 to Fe‐doped MoS 2 , reconfiguring the Mo‐S electronic structure, while simultaneously strengthening Mo─S bonds and suppressing Mo dissolution. Moreover, Fe incorporation is energetically favored at octahedrally coordinated Mo sites within the MoS 2 domain, modulating the local electronic environment of the MoS 2 domain and thereby facilitating coupled electron/ion transport. Consequently, the Fe‐MRS electrode delivers high specific capacitance and excellent cycling stability with a capacitance retention of 97.0% over 5000 cycles. Moreover, asymmetric supercapacitors assembled with the Fe‐MRS anode achieve a high energy density of 55.2 Wh kg −1 at 1000 W kg −1 , maintaining good structural and mechanical robustness. This work offers clear guidance for leveraging selective doping to engineer heterostructures with enhanced electron‐ion coupling for advanced electrochemical energy storage systems.

title: Solvent heterogeneity regulates assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Supramolecular polymers are fundamental mimics of biological assemblies with diverse functions. However, predicting monomer solubility and controlling the colloidal stability of the resulting assemblies in solution remain major challenges. As a result, their preparation commonly relies on solvent mixtures, which can generate local heterogeneities during sample processing—an effect that remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect modulated by monomer structure. Using an amphiphilic Pd(II) complex as a model system, we uncover a thermally accelerated transition from kinetically controlled discrete nanostructures to thermodynamically stable supramolecular polymers in water/1,4-dioxane mixtures. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that this transformation is mediated by microscopic liquid–liquid phase separation within the mixed solvent, creating 1,4-dioxane-enriched microdomains with increased local monomer concentration. Thermal annealing enhances molecular mobility and promotes the growth and coalescence of these microdomains, facilitating the transition to one-dimensional fibers. Extending the investigation to structurally related monomers further identifies the metal center and hydrogen-bonding motifs as key design elements governing this behavior. By linking molecular design and solvent heterogeneity to pathway complexity, our findings highlight how mixed solvents can be used to control supramolecular polymerization.

title: Machine Learning in Liquid Electrolyte Design for Rechargeable Batteries: Addressing Fundamental Challenges
abstract: ABSTRACT Designing high‐performance liquid electrolytes for rechargeable batteries requires simultaneously achieving fast ionic transport, a wide electrochemical window, and interphase stability, yet these objectives are intrinsically coupled and often involve competing trade‐offs. Electrolyte optimization remains a formidable challenge for conventional trial‐and‐error approaches. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) are transforming electrolyte research into a data‐driven and increasingly autonomous paradigm for accelerated materials discovery. This review provides a comprehensive perspective on how ML methodologies are tailored to address the fundamental challenges of liquid electrolyte design. We first introduce the physicochemical foundations of liquid electrolytes alongside key ML workflows, emphasizing dataset construction and feature representation tailored to electrolyte chemistry. We then examine ML strategies for predicting and optimizing ionic transport, electrochemical window, interphase regulation, and multi‐objective optimization, highlighting representative advances and practical design principles for rational electrolyte development. Finally, we discuss current challenges, including data quality, model generalizability, and interpretability, as well as future opportunities for developing mechanism‐informed and transferable ML frameworks. By bridging machine learning with electrolyte science, this review aims to facilitate the rational design of next‐generation liquid electrolytes and accelerate the development of high‐performance rechargeable batteries.

title: Breaking the Boltzmann Limit: A Review of Emerging Ultralow‐Power Transistor Technologies
abstract: ABSTRACT As complementary metal‐oxide‐semiconductor (CMOS) technology scales down to the sub‐2 nm node, the dramatic surge in power density has emerged as a fundamental bottleneck. Conventional metal‐oxide‐semiconductor field‐effect transistors (MOSFETs) are constrained by the 60 mV/dec Boltzmann thermal limit, rendering further supply voltage reduction exceedingly challenging. To surmount this fundamental limit, various novel sub‐60 mV/dec steep‐switching devices have been proposed, including tunnel field‐effect transistors (TFETs), negative‐capacitance field‐effect transistors (NCFETs), and cold‐source field‐effect transistors (CSFETs). A comprehensive review of the evolution of sub‑60 mV/dec technologies is presented, with particular emphasis on the three mainstream approaches: TFETs, NCFETs, and CSFETs. The underlying physical principles, recent research advances, optimization strategies, and remaining challenges of these devices are thoroughly analyzed. Finally, prospective directions for future breakthroughs are discussed, encompassing novel materials exploration, the synergistic integration of multiple physical mechanisms, and the experimental verification of integration with advanced CMOS nodes.

title: High‐Energy and Long‐Life Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 Cathodes via Multielement V‐Site Modulation of Local M–O/F Bonding
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries are promising for sustainable energy storage, but their energy density still lags behind lithium‐ion systems. Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (NVPF) is an attractive high‐voltage polyanionic cathode, but fluorine loss generates low‐voltage Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 impurities that lower energy density and aggravate lattice deformation during cycling. Here, we report a multielement V‐site charge modulation strategy, realized in Na 3‐δ V 1.9 Zr 0.02 Ti 0.02 Cr 0.02 Fe 0.02 Al 0.02 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (ME‐NVPF). The deliberate combination of high‐valence Zr 4+ , Ti 4+ , and same‐valence Cr 3+ , Fe 3+ , Al 3+ cations creates a heterogeneous M–O/F bonding network with multi‐directional electrostatic interactions enhancing lattice‐F retention that completely eliminates NVP impurities, lowers the Na + migration barrier, and reduces unit‐cell volume variation to merely 2.87%. Consequently, ME‐NVPF delivers a record‐high energy density of 477 Wh kg −1 , sustains 11 000 cycles, operates across −40 to 80°C, and is further validated in 600 mAh‐level pouch cells. This work establishes multielement compositional regulation as an effective strategy for designing high‐energy, long‐life, and all‐temperature polyanionic cathodes.

title: Healable Thermoset Elastomeric Materials for Passive Radiative Cooling
abstract: ABSTRACT Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology with zero‐energy uptake is an efficient thermal management strategy for the development of sustainable society. Fabrication of PRC materials with intrinsic extensibility/dimensional stability and efficient healability that can adapt to irregular shapes with prolonged lifetime remains a significant challenge. The present study introduces a design principle for mechanically robust and healable PRC films based on a cross‐linked elastomeric network with combined physical interactions and dynamic covalent bonds, which can be readily modulated by inorganic coating and micro‐/nano‐porous hierarchical architectures while retaining extensibility and healability. Such thermosetting elastomeric PRC films are scalable with strong solar reflectance and long‐wave infrared emittance, realizing excellent cooling performance even after physical damage and healing process. It demonstrates excellent roof cooling ability in summer yet efficient ice‐sculpture preservation function in winter. The scalable synthesis of thermoset elastomeric PRC films opens up new pathways to realize flexible, stable and healable PRC materials, highly promising for practical applications.

title: Robust Sodium–Metal Batteries Through Electrolyte‐Mediated Interfacial Regulation: Fundamentals, Design Strategies, and Operando Characterization
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium–metal batteries (SMBs) exhibit high theoretical specific capacity and take advantage of sodium's natural abundance and low cost, showing great promise for broad next‐generation energy‐storage applications. In this review, we summarize the major practical bottlenecks restricting SMB development. The solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) serves as a key mediator to overcome these challenges, and its formation mechanisms are systematically outlined. We comprehensively review diverse electrolyte strategies, including solvent engineering, salt chemistry optimization, additive utilization, high‐concentration, localized high‐concentration, and weakly solvating electrolytes, for modulating Na + transport and generating mechanically robust, ion‐conductive yet electronically insulating SEI layers. We further discuss advanced in‐situ/operando characterizations combined with multiscale computational modeling and machine‐learning techniques as powerful tools to decipher the dynamic evolution of sodium–metal interfaces. Particular focus is placed on the coupled effects of current density, temperature, electrolyte composition, interfacial layers on sodium nucleation, dendrite growth, dead‐sodium formation, and Coulombic efficiency (CE). Finally, future directions for SEI engineering have been outlook toward high‐performance, practical sodium–metal batteries.

title: A physics-informed deep clustering framework with single-cell voltage features for early fault identification in automotive PEM fuel cell
abstract: In automotive proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), dynamic loads can induce inconsistencies within single cells and localized faults that are challenging to detect using stack-voltage-based diagnostic criteria. To facilitate earlier and more accurate fault identification, a key single-cell feature identification and determination method aimed at early anomaly capture and localization is first developed that quantifies temporal voltage discrepancies and selects the most fault-indicative single cells for diagnostic feature construction. Building on these features, a deep clustering method integrating DenseNet with physics-informed consensus clustering (DPICC) is proposed. Under a semi-supervised framework, a triple physics-informed integration mechanism constrains clustering center initialization, clustering process, and feasibility validation, jointly optimizing representations and cluster structure to improve accuracy and stability with limited labels while relying solely on single-cell voltage features. Experimental results demonstrate that fault identification can be advanced by up to approximately 35 s versus stack-voltage-based methods. Compared with Support Vector Machine (SVM), DPICC improves accuracy by 6.03%, and generalizes better across operating conditions. Ablations confirm that the triple physics-informed mechanism enhances clustering stability and interpretability, yielding an overall gain of approximately 16.6%. The proposed method provides a feasible pathway for early fault identification and reliable diagnosis of automotive PEMFCs.

title: Hydrogen integration for sustainable aviation propulsion: Evaluating recirculation efficiency in PEMFC systems
A GPU-accelerated multi-physics coupling framework based on the lattice boltzmann method for performance analysis of utility-scale photovoltaic power plants
An interpretable aging prediction model for Ni-rich all-solid-state batteries informed by mechanistic modeling
abstract: Ni-rich all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage technology, while they suffer from much more severe capacity fading than lithium-ion batteries with liquid electrolyte, severely compromising their practical application and commercialization. Accurate degradation prediction is required to improve the operational stability of Ni-rich ASSBs. A novel degradation prediction framework for NCA (LiNi 0.8 Co 0.16 Al 0.03 , Nickel content: 80%) cathode ASSBs is proposed based on a mechanism model combined with deep neural network in this study. This study first constructs a three-dimensional physical model of ASSBs with NCA cathodes. On the basis of experimental observations, three cathode capacity degradation processes, namely interfacial side reactions, interfacial delamination and particle cracking, are parameterized. Subsequently, the CNN-LSTM hybrid framework is constructed for model training, and a multi-level prediction module is further embedded into the architecture to leverage the advantage of physical model in capturing battery internal characteristics, e.g., the Li concentration as an additional feature. Validated by simulation data, the proposed model possesses the high prediction accuracy in estimating NCA-based ASSBs degradation. Comparative analyses are carried out against the prediction model without concentration correction to further verify the rationality of the proposed prediction framework, indicating that concentration correction substantially enhances the prediction accuracy under small-sample scenarios. The three-dimensional mechanism model-neural network fusion framework proposed in this work verifies that neural networks embedded with physical prior information such as lithium-ion concentration exhibit stronger learning capacity. Even under limited data conditions, the framework can accurately predict capacity degradation of ASSBs with NCA cathodes. This study provides theoretical references for performance prediction and battery management of NCA-based ASSBs.

title: Assessing behavior-conditioned building flexibility potential across building types for photovoltaic accommodation
abstract: Building flexibility is increasingly recognized as an important demand-side resource for renewable energy integration, yet its characterization in real buildings remains challenging because flexibility is strongly conditioned by operational behavior and is difficult to quantify without detailed system information. This study proposes a behavior-informed framework to assess behavior-conditioned flexibility potential across building types using historical operation data, and further examines its potential implications for photovoltaic (PV) accommodation under building-cluster scenarios. Using 15-min measured electricity data from multiple types of public buildings in Hangzhou, China, the framework first establishes baseline load behavior through quantile-based modeling, then identifies feasible operating ranges from historically comparable operating conditions, and finally estimates behavior-conditioned flexibility potential in terms of both instantaneous adjustable power and duration-based adjustable energy. XGBoost-SHAP analysis is further employed to interpret the statistical associations between input features and the estimated flexibility indicators, and an aggregated analysis is conducted to evaluate the value of flexibility potential for PV accommodation under different curtailment constraints. For the studied public-building dataset, the estimated flexibility potential shows clear heterogeneity across building types. Load level, hour of day, outdoor temperature, and daily load characteristics show the largest contributions to the model predictions, suggesting that the estimated flexibility potential is closely associated with energy-consuming behavior. At the cluster level, the results further reveal that high flexibility does not necessarily translate into high PV accommodation potential. Under a 15% curtailment threshold, the average PV capacity factor of the realistic mixed-building aggregation scenario increased from 0.288 to 0.369 in the flexibility-enhanced scenario, corresponding to an absolute increase of 0.08 and a relative improvement of 27.9%. Across different aggregation capacity levels, the relative improvement in PV accommodation ranged from 23% to 30%. These results indicate that the cluster-level value of flexibility depends strongly on the temporal match between flexible load patterns and PV generation. This study provides a scalable data-driven approach for characterizing building flexibility from historical operational data and offers new insights into the potential contribution of behavior-conditioned flexibility to renewable energy integration and building-cluster planning under specified scenarios.

title: Synchronic Multilevel Assembly Toward Mesoporous Nanosized Intercalation‐Type Framework Anodes for Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Intercalation‐type metal oxides are promising anodes for fast‐charging sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, viable electrode candidates remain scarce, constituting a major bottleneck and motivating intensive research into diverse structural frameworks. Here, we report a synchronic multilevel assembly strategy for synthesizing mesoporous intercalation‐type metal oxide framework anodes. Atomic‐scale assembly of cations, combined with in situ formation of conductive carbon networks, enables the synthesis of structurally tunable nanosized sodium titanate and overcomes the challenges of preparing multimetal oxide nanocrystals under high temperatures. The M‐Na 4 Ti 5 O 12 /C composite delivers superior rate capability (∼115 mAh g −1 at 10 A g −1 ) and cycling stability (−1 ) for sodium storage. Its outstanding kinetics arise from ultrafast Na + diffusion through interconnected mesoporous channels and low‐barrier, nanoscale ion‐conduction pathways. A pouch cell delivers a power density of ∼4.7 kW kg −1 and cycles stably for 1200 cycles, outperforming hard carbon at high rates. This work establishes a rational design framework for developing high‐rate battery materials.

title: Revealing inter-cell water-gas-coupled transfer characteristics and degradation-driven evolution within large-scale fuel cell stacks
abstract: Hydrophobicity decay is a critical driving force behind the degradation of proton exchange membrane fuel cells. However, the cross-scale linkage between microscopic material-level hydrophobic degradation and macroscopic stack-level water-gas transfer behaviors remains largely obscure, as well as the further inducing consequences. Bridging the gap, this study reveals the inter-cell water-gas-coupled transfer characteristics and degradation-driven evolution within large-scale fuel cell stacks. Applying the micro-current excitation method on a 60-cell stack, the evolution of membrane electrode assembly (MEA) material states is recognized after the 1000-h durability test. Except for typical catalyst degradation, an anomalous degradation feature is captured, wherein hydrophobicity degradation facilitates internal water accumulation and reduces ohmic resistance, consequently leading to the performance rise in ohmic polarization region. The degradation inconsistency within stack is found to be correlated with flow maldistribution. At the inter-cell level, cells with lower flow rates suffer from more severe degradation due to water accumulation and potential air starvation, which is especially pronounced in end cells. At the intra-cell in-plane level, the hydrophobicity degradation of MEA at the air downstream region is also more serious. For stacks assembled with MEAs with different hydrophobic states driven by degradation, the internal water accumulation difference and inter-cell coupling effect combine to cause gas redistribution. The evolution of gas distribution with humidity clearly indicates that the tendency of water accumulation within degraded cells increases the flow resistance and decreases the flow rate under high humidity conditions. Consequently, degraded MEAs suffer a greater risk of water flooding and significant deterioration in dynamic response performance, which forms a vicious cycle of accelerated degradation. This study enriches the cross-scale degradation mechanism theory of fuel cell stacks and holds significant values for consistency guarantee and lifetime extension.

title: MERIF: a market-informed electricity-price risk and interval forecasting framework for renewable-rich power markets
abstract: Renewable-rich electricity markets combine persistent temporal structure with negative prices, rapid volatility, and rare scarcity spikes, requiring forecasts that address price level, uncertainty, and upper-tail exposure. This study proposes the Market-informed Electricity-price Risk and Interval Forecasting Framework (MERIF), integrating tail-aware stacked quantile regression (TSQR), complete-day rolling conformalized quantile regression (RCQR), and support-aware extreme-risk monitoring (XRM). MERIF was estimated independently in the DE-LU, DK1, BE, ES, and FR bidding zones and evaluated on 15,311 common held-out hourly products per market using strictly pre-issuance price-calendar information. TSQR reduced mean absolute error by 3.09–12.82% relative to persistence and by 0.91–2.48% relative to stacked quantile regression. Raw 80% interval coverage of 0.578–0.717 increased to 0.796–0.805 after the 60-day RCQR update, while interval score fell by 2.80–11.87 EUR/MWh. Adding archived day-ahead system forecasts further reduced TSQR error by 7.5–26.9%. At the primary P95 event definition, the TSQR q0.50 and q0.90 forecasts provided strong ranking benchmarks, while XRM added a continuous support-aware diagnostic. Across five markets, MERIF consistently strengthened central forecasting and marginal interval reliability while providing an evidence-aware route to upper-tail monitoring.

title: Continuous health monitoring of solid oxide electrolyzers using pulse-width modulation current interrupt analysis
abstract: As solid oxide electrolyzer (SOE) technology moves from button cells to commercial stacks, there is a growing need for fast and inexpensive methods to track the stack’s state-of-health during operation. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is the standard diagnostic at the lab scale, but the cost, current limitations, and test duration of frequency-response analyzers make routine EIS measurements impractical for large stacks/systems. To address this problem, pulse-width modulation is combined with current-interrupt analysis (PWM-CI) to achieve continuous, in-situ monitoring of SOE health. The proposed PWM-CI method utilizes the “off” portion of the PWM cycle (when the applied voltage to the cell is removed) to perform rapid current interrupt measurements and analyzes the resulting voltage transients using a developed state-space model that explicitly accounts for cable inductance, switch capacitance, and oscilloscope properties. A fitting framework is developed that extracts ohmic, polarization, and total resistances from individual interrupts using only 50 ms of voltage decay, while avoiding the multi-minute interruption of hydrogen production required for EIS. PWM-CI tracking of button cells over 500 h generates ohmic resistances and time constants in agreement with EIS and distribution-of-relaxation-times analysis respectively, and accurately captures the degradation trends. The PWM-CI method is further demonstrated on a 45-cell commercial technology demonstrator stack, where inductive and capacitive effects cause oscillatory transients that are accounted for using the state-space model. After calibration of the electronic parasitics, PWM-CI yields stable resistance and time-constant estimates over 957 h of stack operation. The developed PWM-CI approach provides a practical pathway toward continuous health monitoring of SOE stacks under realistic dynamic operating conditions.

title: A two-layer safe deep reinforcement learning framework for coordinated control of radiative cooling envelopes and HVAC systems
abstract: Integrating passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) envelopes into buildings is an effective strategy for reducing cooling energy demand. However, due to their limited cooling capacity, HVAC systems remain necessary to maintain indoor thermal comfort. The performance of PDRC envelopes is strongly influenced by meteorological conditions, limiting the effectiveness of conventional rule-based control strategies. To address this, a two-layer safe deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework is proposed to coordinate PDRC envelopes and HVAC systems for enhanced energy savings while maintaining thermal comfort. In the training layer, a Lagrange multiplier is incorporated into the reward function to dynamically penalize comfort violations, enabling the agent to learn a weather-adaptive trade-off between comfort and energy use. In the deployment layer, a physics-based predictor and optimizer is used to reduce the risk of thermal comfort violations. A comparative study of building energy performance under different control strategies is conducted. Results show that PDRC envelopes significantly reduce the interior surface temperatures of roofs and walls, improving thermal comfort even at the same indoor air temperature. Compared with rule-based control, the proposed framework further reduces cooling-season electricity consumption and cost by 12.1% and 13.5%, respectively, while also outperforming standard DRL control in thermal comfort. This study provides new insight into intelligent control of buildings with PDRC envelopes.

title: Global green hydrogen site suitability and cost competitiveness: an open-source geospatial and uncertainty assessment across 182 countries
abstract: Green hydrogen facility siting is commonly guided either by techno-economic cost minimization or by multi-criteria suitability assessment, yet the extent to which these approaches identify the same development priorities remains unclear. A site that can produce low-cost green hydrogen may not necessarily be suitable. Here, we develop an open-source, spatially explicit framework covering 182 countries that applies both approaches independently to a common technically eligible land base. The framework's methodological novelty lies in independently applying cost minimization and multi-criteria suitability assessment to a common eligible land base, enabling a consistent spatial comparison of cost-optimal and highly suitable locations while integrating spatial exclusions, hourly solar and wind generation modelling, plant-gate levelized cost of hydrogen estimation, spatial water-supply pathways, and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. Spatial exclusions reduce globally eligible land to 40%. Solar is the least-cost option across 81% of eligible areas, whereas wind-dominated locations achieve a lower median hydrogen cost of $2.8/kg compared with $3.1/kg for solar. However, it was demonstrated that the lowest-cost locations do not consistently coincide with the highest-suitability areas. These findings show that cost competitiveness and development suitability are related but non-equivalent, and that their combined assessment provides a more robust basis for prioritizing large-scale green hydrogen production.

title: Coordinated operation of Mobile substations and multiple Mobile flexible resources in coupled power distribution and transportation networks
Passive anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation: From mechanisms to applications
abstract: Frost formation in low-temperature environments causes significant efficiency losses and safety hazards across aerospace, HVAC, and manufacturing industries. Conventional active anti-frosting methods suffer from poor energy efficiency due to periodic energy input requirements. This review summarizes recent advances in passive anti-frosting through interfacial humidity regulation—a strategy that inhibits ice crystal nucleation and growth by actively controlling local water vapor, offering substantial energy-saving potential. We firstly discuss theoretical models of ice nucleation in supersaturated vapor, examining how surface energy, microstructure, and chemistry govern interfacial humidity distribution and phase transitions. Secondly, three widely reported humidity regulating media, ice, hygroscopic gels, and hygroscopic liquids, are examined in terms of their vapor regulation mechanisms and frost suppression performance. Thirdly, we address advanced anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation via hygroscopic materials, biological protein and inspired microstructured surfaces. This review provides theoretical foundations and technical guidance for next-generation energy-efficient frost suppression technologies.

title: Beyond nature: charting the roadmap to intelligent biomanufacturing for sustainable biohydrogen
A comprehensive review of global advanced metering infrastructure cost-benefit evidence and a data-integration framework for master-metered high-voltage apartment complexes
abstract: Advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) is the core sensing layer of decarbonizing grids, but its value is realized only where interval data reach the grid operator and the tariff setter. This review synthesizes three separate literatures: the functional evolution of metering; cross-national AMI cost-benefit analyses (CBAs) covering Europe, Japan and South Korea; and data governance in master-metered multi-occupancy buildings. Deconstructing CBA formulations shows that only labor substitution accrues directly from meter installation; every other benefit category depends on coefficients that require data reachability. This helps account for the order-of-magnitude dispersion in benefit–cost ratios, which is associated more closely with the evaluation boundary and complementary institutions than with technology cost, and exposes a structural vulnerability in South Korea. Deployment reached 20 million low-voltage customers in 2024 (B/C 1.03), yet the 11.96 million households in 28,253 high-voltage apartment complexes largely sit outside the metering data pipeline: the complex, not the household, is the contracting customer, and household meters are private assets behind the supply point. AMI hardware reaches 53% of these households but only 15.4% (1.84 million) are linked to the utility, leaving 4.5 million households whose interval data reach a private server and go no further. The exclusion became binding in 2026, when residential time-of-use (TOU) tariffs were deferred nationally for want of AMI coverage. Japan’s Specified Metering (IoT-route) system, Australia’s embedded networks and North American master metering show that such arrangements can be made useful without dissolving supply contracts. We propose a conceptual, hypothesis-generating architecture for an apartment-dedicated meter data management system (APT-MDMS) with gateway-based integration, server-side TOU settlement, a consent and privacy architecture, and a five-year, four-segment roadmap. The proposed architecture and roadmap are design hypotheses whose system interfaces, reliability, costs and economic viability require pilot validation.

title: Co-optimizing revenue generation and lifetime degradation of lithium-ion batteries in energy markets using physics-based modeling
Dual Single Atoms Boosting Photocatalytic Upcycling of Raw Polyvinylidene Fluoride Plastic
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a highly recalcitrant fluorinated polymer that is highly resistant to chemical degradation, making its sustainable recycling and upcycling challenging. Despite its widespread use as a binder in the lithium‐ion battery industry, effective strategies for converting PVDF waste into value‐added chemicals remain limited. To resolve this, Fe and Cu dual single atoms incorporated on a new two‐dimensional material nanosheets (In 2 P 3 S 9 NSs/Fe‐Cu DSAs) were prepared as photocatalysts for direct raw PVDF plastic conversion to high‐value chemicals. The best‐performing photocatalyst (Fe 1.0 Cu 0.5 ) achieves a total acetic/formic acid generation of ∼1351.8 µmol g −1 . Various in situ characterizations such as atomic force microscopy‐kelvin probe force microscopy, x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) demonstrate superior electron extraction from In 2 P 3 S 9 NSs to Fe and Cu DSAs, after which the electrons are subsequently scavenged by O 2 under ambient conditions. Moreover, quenching experiments as well as in situ infrared spectroscopy, and in situ EPR reveal the vital impact of photoexcited electrons and hydroxyl radicals in PVDF upcycling into high‐value products. These findings highlight the significant potential of photocatalysis in transforming one of the most resistant plastic wastes (PVDF) into value‐added products, providing a sustainable remedy for plastic pollution crisis.

title: Graph neural networks for transmission grid topology control: Busbar information asymmetry and heterogeneous representations
Maximising self-consumption in energy communities: a comparative study of demand flexibility and dynamic sharing strategies
abstract: Energy Communities (ECs) have emerged as a vehicle for actively engaging citizens in the energy transition, enabling them to generate, consume, store and share renewable energy. Maximising collective self-consumption is a key objective of ECs, as it allows members to better capture the benefits of shared energy generation, and several approaches have been developed toward this goal. However, most of existing works aim to maximise ECs’ self-consumption by applying demand side management strategies or increasing the benefits with dynamic energy sharing, but not combining them. This study is one of the first to propose a data-driven framework that leverages machine learning, optimisation, battery management and dynamic energy sharing strategies to increase the self-consumption of ECs. The impact of the optimisation and dynamic energy sharing coefficients on ECs’ self-consumption and electricity costs was examined, together with their combination. The application of the proposed framework to an established Renewable Energy Community (REC) in Spain shows that dynamic energy sharing yields better results compared to load optimisation, and their combination shows more promising results. Permitting more frequent updates of dynamic energy-sharing coefficients can improve the allocation of locally generated energy and support higher member-level self-consumption, particularly in communities with heterogeneous and seasonal demand profiles.

title: Durable Interphase Incorporating Cross‐Linked Polymer Enables Long‐Calendar‐Life Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The practical deployment of lithium (Li) metal batteries is hindered by not only cycle life but also calendar life. The poor calendar life stems from both the repeated reconstruction of the solid‐electrolyte interphase (SEI) during cycles and, particularly, the continuous growth of SEI during storage. Herein, a durable SEI with high mechanical stability against volume fluctuations and superior passivation capability to suppress electrolyte permeation is demonstrated by integrating inorganics and a cross‐linked polymer into the SEI. Concretely, a cross‐linked polymer with high modulus and low swelling is in‐situ incorporated among the inorganics of an anion‐derived SEI. The elastic modulus of the SEI is significantly increased from 1.63 to 4.37 GPa, and the compactness of the SEI is also improved to suppress electrolyte permeation. Consequently, the cycle life and calendar life of Li metal coin cells are extended by 73% (from 190 to 329 cycles) and 129% (from 1553 to 3561 h), respectively. Furthermore, a prototype pouch cell (506 Wh kg −1 ) undergoes 124 cycles. This work establishes an effective strategy that concurrently improves the mechanical and passivation performance of the SEI, tackling the critical challenge of calendar life in Li metal batteries.

title: Energy policy and energy poverty under geopolitical fragmentation: Evidence on structural constraints
Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

title: Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
abstract: The 2022 energy price shock, triggered by geopolitical disruptions, prompted governments to implement widespread policy interventions to support firms and accelerate the energy transition. Using nationally representative firm surveys from the United States and Germany, this paper examines how firms adjusted to the shock and their reported responses to fiscal incentives. We document that firms were generally resilient, relying on a combination of price pass-through, margin adjustment, and energy-saving investments. Responses differed across countries: firms in Germany – facing a larger and more persistent shock – were more likely to invest in energy efficiency and reduce energy consumption, while firms in the United States primarily absorbed costs through lower profits. Evidence from input-output simulations suggests that, absent policy intervention, energy-intensive sectors would have faced substantially larger price pressures. We also find that firms with pre-existing plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions were more likely to report intending to utilize fiscal incentive programs, suggesting that policy targeting and credibility may play an important role in supporting the green transition. Overall, our findings provide descriptive evidence on firms’ responses to energy price shocks and announced policy measures, offering insights for the design of targeted and predictable energy and climate policies in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical environment.

title: Circular economy practices and clean energy transition performance: the moderating role of critical mineral circularity and policy stringency among EU energy-intensive firms
Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: Translating EU renewable energy community policy under geopolitical constraint: An actor-network analysis of Cyprus
Accurately modeling long-term storage with minimum representative hours in large-scale renewable energy systems
abstract: Energy system optimization often relies on time series aggregation to ensure computational tractability. Aggregation generally loses the chronology of time steps, which renders the storage level representation challenging. Typically, this challenge is addressed by using representative days (RD) to utilize intra-day chronology, even though representative hours (RH) can describe the input time series more accurately at fewer representative time steps than RD. However, until now, the use of RH storage representation methods has been limited by either high computational complexity, poor accuracy in clustering and storage representation, or restricted applicability. Here, we present a novel storage representation method based on RH that combines the high accuracy of RH time series aggregation with the high computational efficiency of methods based on RD. Through benchmarking the four most established storage representation methods on a model of a net-zero European energy system, we find that the proposed method can reduce the solving time by over 95% for the same objective value compared to the most established RD and RH methods. The proposed method exhibits particular strengths at strong aggregations of around 100 to 500 representative hours per year, making the method especially applicable to large-scale and sector-coupled transition pathway models. The developed method for accurately modeling both short-term and long-term storage, along with the presented findings, is of practical relevance to energy system modelers who seek computational tractability in large-scale applications while avoiding the misallocation of storage and conversion capacities.

title: Epeditor: A scalable platform for large-ensemble building energy simulation enabling agent-assisted automation
abstract: The data scale of energy simulation keeps increasing, particularly in urban building energy modeling (UBEM) and uncertainty analysis, where thousands of EnergyPlus runs are often required to explore complex parameter spaces and building variability. To simplify these data-intensive workflows, recent studies have introduced AI agents for end-to-end simulation tasks. However, in practice, both AI-assisted and conventional batch workflows remain constrained by unstable field inference and search bias, inefficient large-ensemble simulation execution, and cumbersome data processing. To address these problems, this study introduces Epeditor, a cloud-deployable simulation infrastructure for large-ensemble building energy analysis for both AI and human users. It combines three improvements on current workflows: a knowledge-assisted parameterization with more accurate and stable field search in IDF files; a simulator that improves parallel execution efficiency through Operating-System-Level deployment; and a data management system that enables memory-safe aggregation of large simulation inputs and outputs. The packaged Agent Skill allows AI agents to execute fully automated dataset generation, batch simulation, surrogate modeling, and interpretation through an auditable workflow. Epeditor is evaluated through a agent benchmarks with metrics for Artificial General Intelligence, and two case studies are introduced to show its ability in research and design practices including an AI-assisted surrogate-modeling case, and design-studio practices. The pipeline exhibits 99.98% robustness in IDF generation, up to four-fold acceleration in high-parallel simulation, and 76.28 ( F 1 ) in IDF field inference. These findings indicate that Epeditor can lower the technical and computational barriers to large-ensemble EnergyPlus simulation, supporting more accessible, reproducible, and AI-ready building energy analysis.

title: Strategic scenario planning for hydrogen supply chains via graph convolutional networks: overcoming mid-stream infrastructure bottlenecks in energy transitions
abstract: : Hydrogen transitions require a combination of change in policy, production, distribution, and adoption, but current scenario consistency assessment only checks for trend coherence without incorporating the role of the relationships among the stakeholders in shaping those emerging pathways. This study introduces a Graph Convolutional Network-based Scenario Planning (GCN-SP) framework that extends scenario-consistency assessment by linking actor-node engagement with emerging trends to graph-based representations of representative hydrogen scenarios. Multi-driver interaction effects are transformed into strategic scenario graphs, clustered using k-means to derive representative configurations from cluster centroids, and classified using a graph convolutional network. The optimal model achieves weighted precision and recall exceeding 0.78 under both cross-validation and hold-out validation and outperforms two multilayer perceptron baselines. Three distinct structural configurations emerge. Coordinated: aligned actors across government, production, distribution, and adoption form a mutually reinforcing structure supporting system integration. Divergent: production and international connectivity advance while the producer becomes disconnected from the domestic network, creating an export-oriented pathway. Constrained: supply-side ambition and transport expansion outpace downstream adoption, leaving the value chain incomplete. Across scenarios, distribution emerges as a structurally important link whose connectivity determines whether production translates into integration. These results show that similar stakeholder activity can generate fundamentally different outcomes depending on interaction configuration. GCN-SP therefore enables structural distinction between coordinated integration, export-oriented divergence, and supply-led constraint.

title: A stochastic techno-economic framework for hydrogen-based maritime decarbonisation under market and policy uncertainty
Node-aware spatiotemporal carbon tracing and carbon-responsive control of electrified railways for emission reduction and tertiary reserves
abstract: The decarbonization of electrified transportation reshapes the interaction between power systems and mobile energy loads. As a key component of this sector, electrified railways draw large, geographically distributed traction loads whose emissions are governed by the power system’s spatiotemporally varying carbon intensity (CI). However, existing carbon tracing methods typically use spatially uniform emission factors, obscuring nodal carbon intensity (CI) differences. Consequently, long-distance trains cannot perceive or exploit spatial carbon heterogeneity when allocating traction power along their routes. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a unified framework that transforms heterogeneous railway fleets into active, carbon-responsive resources within the power system. First, a node-aware spatiotemporal carbon tracing method integrates Power Transfer Distribution Factors (PTDF) with dynamic train-node mapping, enabling real-time quantification of the nodal carbon intensity (NCI) experienced by mobile loads. Building upon this, a two-stage hierarchical coordinated control strategy is formulated, embedding dynamic NCI signals into an online receding-horizon predictive controller to achieve joint carbon minimization and tertiary reserve. The controller autonomously executes spatiotemporal load shifting by dynamically regulating traction and braking power to avoid high-carbon zones while maintaining schedule adherence. Case studies on high-speed and freight railways demonstrate that traditional system-average carbon accounting systematically obscures local low-carbon zones, overestimating the fleet’s true carbon footprint by more than four times under severe spatiotemporal mismatch. By actively exploiting these spatial zero-carbon opportunities, the proposed NCI-aware control achieves substantial carbon reductions, of 37.14% for high-speed trains and 34.74% for freight trains, while maintaining schedule adherence. Crucially, the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition reveals that these emission mitigations originate predominantly from the strategic utilization of low-carbon nodes, rather than mere energy conservation. These results demonstrate a promising framework for integrated power–transport system decarbonization, transforming electrified railways from passive loads into active carbon-aware grid participants.

title: Adaptive dead-zone dual sliding mode observer for reliable electrochemical model-based SOC estimation
abstract: Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is essential for safe and efficient lithium-ion battery operation. Electrochemical models provide physically grounded SOC estimates, but nonlinear voltage dynamics and coupled state-parameter errors can destabilize online adaptation. This paper proposes an adaptive dead-zone dual sliding-mode observer (ADZ-DSMO) based on an improved extended single-particle (IESP) model. A state SMO estimates SOC-related states, while a parameter SMO updates dominant model parameters. An online-computable, Lyapunov-guided adaptive boundary selectively gates parameter updates while the state observer remains active at every sampling step. Validation on a Panasonic NCR18650PF cell under 1C and 3C constant-current discharge and the Urban Dynamometer Driving Schedule (UDDS) and New European Driving Cycle (NEDC) profiles shows lower SOC estimation errors than conventional dual SMO and the IESP-based dual extended Kalman filter (DEKF). Compared with DEKF, the proposed observer provides faster recovery from a 30% initial SOC bias. Selective parameter updating reduces the average per-step computation time compared with the always-updating dual SMO. Temperature tests and capacity-based, model-generated aging cases further assess robustness. These results support adaptive gating as a means of reducing error propagation and computational overhead in electrochemical-model-based joint state-parameter estimation.

title: A reference-electrode-free adaptive AC heating framework for lithium-ion batteries accounting for cold-spot temperature prediction
abstract: Low-temperature environments severely degrade the discharge capability of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and induce lithium plating during charging, leading to irreversible capacity loss. To address these challenges, this study proposes a reference-electrode-free adaptive AC heating framework, which is built on a fractional-order electro-thermal coupling model and integrates physics-constrained neural network (PCNN) parameter estimation, cold-spot temperature prediction, and a multi-constraint formulation module. The PCNN achieved parameter identification with a maximum MARE of 5.46% despite limited training samples. Supported by these adaptive parameters, the coupling model predicted terminal voltage and lumped temperature accurately, with a voltage root-mean-square error (RMSE) below 25 mV and a temperature error below 0.45 °C. To ensure safety under local lithium-plating risk, a cold-spot temperature prediction module was developed to estimate the minimum temperature with a 3.6% error, in combination with electrochemical analysis to establish a local lithium-plating boundary without requiring reference electrodes, which is further integrated with terminal voltage and equipment limits for excitation optimization. Experimental results demonstrated stable and efficient heating at −30 °C. Under a 4C current limit, the heating rate was increased by 6.6% compared with the existing cut-off frequency strategy. Moreover, the capacity degradation remained below 1% after 80 heating cycles even at I equip = 6C. Overall, this work provides a practical framework to determine excitation under multiple safety constraints for reference-electrode-free LIBs in extreme climates, incorporating cold-spot temperature prediction to ensure localized safety.

title: Mechanisms of capacity decay in iron‑chromium flow batteries: unraveling the role of electrolyte imbalance
abstract: The imbalance in iron‑chromium mixed electrolytes is a major cause of capacity decay in iron‑chromium flow batteries (ICFBs). This study proposes an electrolyte state model that examines the impact of molar and valent imbalances on the theoretical capacity of ICFBs using molar-based formulations. The model correlates the extent of valent imbalance with the capacity of an iron ion concentration cell (IICC), a specialized operational mode of ICFBs. In this mode, valent imbalance worsens primarily due to oxygen intrusion, which motivates us to quantify the O 2 intrusion rate by leveraging the capacity evolution of the IICC. During normal operation, electrolyte imbalance also arises from the parasitic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and the crossover of energy-bearing species.
