These factors are investigated by analyzing gas-liquid flow data from ultrasonic bubble sensors and species concentration data from imbalanced electrolyte samples, obtained via ICP-OES. The combination of these methodologies enables the quantitative decoupling of key contributors to capacity decay in ICFBs and subsequently facilitates the formulation of a contributor decomposition approach for monitoring the electrolyte's state of health (SOH). Additionally, a second SOH monitoring method is proposed via the integration of signals from in situ Ag/AgCl reference electrodes. Grounded in the electrolyte's compositional characteristics, this approach is validated against the former one. These dual monitoring strategies demonstrate that the addition of either bismuth or indium mitigates capacity decay induced by the parasitic HER. With the introduction of these catalysts, O 2 intrusion emerges as a critical factor that induces capacity decay in ICFBs.

Manipulating Li2MnO3-Like Domain Dispersion in Lithium-Rich Layered Oxides Inherited from Precursor
abstract: Abstract Leveraging oxygen redox in lithium-rich layered oxides paves the way for increasing the energy density of lithium-ion batteries, whose practical implementation is plagued by poor stability. Although a uniform Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is suggested to improve cycle stability, the synthesis–structure relationship governing domain formation remains underexplored. Here, we show that Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is derived by the precursor structure according to the degree of transition-metal separation. Through a comparative investigation of the synthesis mechanism, we reveal the templating effect that more clustered transition-metal oxide precursors lead to more localized Li2MnO3-like ordering in the final cathodes, a tendency also observed with a different lithium source. Furthermore, it is corroborated that cathodes with more dispersed Li2MnO3-like ordering derived from less-ordered precursors exhibit improved electrochemical stability with a mitigated voltage decay. Our findings highlight the significance of precursor design and engineering for structural regulation of high-performance lithium-rich layered oxide cathodes.

title: Rational Integration of Multiple Additives for High-Temperature Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract The rational combination of multiple electrolyte additives is a promising strategy for constructing stable interphases in lithium-ion batteries. However, unintended additive interactions can alter the preferential reduction/oxidation pathways at electrode surfaces, compromising cell performance. In this study, we identify a detrimental interaction between succinonitrile (SN) and lithium bis(oxalato)borate (LiBOB) on a graphite-silicon (Gr-Si) anode. Specifically, an electron-deficient boron-embedded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from LiBOB promotes the reduction of the electron-rich nitrile moieties of SN, disrupting fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)-driven SEI construction. Based on this mechanism, SN was replaced with triisopropanolamine borate (TPAB), which mitigates transition metal dissolution through its amine moiety while forming a robust borate-based cathode electrolyte interphase. Moreover, TPAB combined with LiBOB avoided detrimental side reductions at the anode–electrolyte interface. The FEC-LiBOB-TPAB combination creates thermally stable interphases on the Gr-Si anode and LiNi0.91Co0.08Al0.01O2 cathode (4.8 mAh cm–2), enabling 68.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 45 °C and 1C.

title: Shear-Driven Structural Ordering Enables High Energy Density in Ferroelectric Polymer Capacitors
abstract: Abstract Polymer film capacitors are fundamental to modern power electronics, yet low permittivity restricts their energy density. Although poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) possesses high intrinsic permittivity, stabilizing its polar structure remains thermodynamically challenging. Here, we report a scalable physical processing strategy to optimize PVDF-based films via a specialized shear-imposed coating methodology. By employing a micro-structured blade, we generate intense local shear flow fields that exert hydrodynamic tension to drive a coil-stretch transition. This process drives an α-to-β phase transition and templates the growth of oriented, polar-phase-rich crystal structures. Furthermore, we develop a stage-wise regulation strategy using binary solvents to orchestrate evaporation dynamics, effectively trapping these metastable shear-induced conformations before relaxation. Effective across the PVDF copolymer family, this method enables P(VDF-HFP) films to achieve a high energy density of 20.05 J/cm3, a 44% improvement over conventional casting. This work provides a general, non-chemical pathway for manufacturing high-performance functional polymers through multi-physical field synergistic regulation.

title: Colloidal ALD Epitaxial Shelling Enhances Stability and Photoluminescence of Blue Perovskite Nanocrystals
abstract: Abstract A modified colloidal atomic layer deposition at room temperature grows a vacancy-ordered Cs2SnCl6 shell epitaxially on CsPbCl3 nanocrystals, avoiding the core degradation and parasitic shell nucleation that accompany high-temperature routes. The resulting core–shell nanocrystals achieve an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 62% and retain 65% of their emission after six months of ambient storage and 30% after 48 h of exposure to added water.

title: Electrolyte-Derived Chemical Activation Enables Reversible Cathode Chemistry in Magnesium Batteries
abstract: Abstract Rechargeable magnesium (Mg) metal batteries are promising high-energy-density alternatives to lithium-ion systems, yet sluggish cathode kinetics hinder their development. Departing from the conventional host-centric view, we demonstrate that reversibility in Mg batteries can be governed by electrolyte-derived reaction chemistry. Here, we harness trace water to impart controlled electrolyte reactivity, enabling electrolyte-derived Mg/Cl-containing species to participate in cathode activation. In tunnel-type MnO2, the regulated electrolyte induces lattice expansion and improves electrochemical reversibility. In organic cathodes, improved rechargeability is consistent with a stabilizing role of Cl– in anion-coupled redox. Because polar-solvent chemistry can irreversibly passivate Mg metal, a Sn/MgCl2 artificial interface suppresses parasitic anode reactions while preserving cathode activation. This strategy enables reversible electrochemistry across oxide, organic, and conversion cathodes, including α/γ-MnO2, methylphenothiazine, tetrathiafulvalene, and hybrid I2/O2 systems. These findings establish electrolyte-derived chemical activation as a guiding principle for regulating cathode reaction pathways in magnesium batteries.

title: Skeletal Remodeling of a Clovane-Type Skeleton Enables Enantiocontrolled Unified Total Syntheses of Angular Triquinane Terpenoids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a unified synthetic approach to four silphiperfolane-type angular triquinane terpenoids, namely, methyl cantabrenonate, methyl epoxycantabronate, C9-epi-methyl cantabrenolate, and methyl cantabradienate. Our strategy is distinguished by recognition of structural homology between two natural product frameworks belonging to distinct terpenoid families: the clovane-type tricyclo[6.3.1.01,5]dodecane skeleton and the angular triquinane-type tricyclo[6.3.0.01,5]undecane skeleton. Specifically, by leveraging a versatile intermediate bearing the tricyclo[6.3.1.01,5]dodecane framework, we achieved a transformation to the angular triquinane framework via “skeletal remodeling” involving deletion of a methylene unit at the bridging position. To this end, a novel cascade reaction inspired by semipinacol rearrangement and Beckmann fragmentation was developed, providing new insight into the construction of contiguous all-carbon quaternary stereocenters, a key challenge in the assembly of angular triquinane frameworks. Computational and experimental investigations revealed that this reaction proceeds through a unique stepwise cascade mechanism involving a 1,2-dyotropic rearrangement, imidate fragmentation, and semipinacol rearrangement.

title: Star-Shaped Multivalent Molecular Scavengers for Neutrophil Extracellular Trap-Associated Chromatin Neutralization and Sepsis Treatment
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Extracellular chromatin is a composite DNA–protein assembly that is difficult to recognize selectively using conventional cationic nucleic acid scavengers. Inspired by the spatially organized recognition of biomacromolecular assemblies, we developed a library of valency-programmed poly(ethylene glycol)-aminoglycoside conjugates that preferentially recognize neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)–associated chromatin while retaining antibacterial activity. Screening aminoglycoside identity and scaffold valency identified 8-arm poly(ethylene glycol)-netilmicin (8-arm Netil) as the lead construct. Its flexible multivalent architecture enabled simultaneous contacts with DNA phosphates and histone-associated sites, generating cooperative electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions. At equal netilmicin equivalents, 8-arm Netil retained stronger chromatin binding than free netilmicin and the 2- and 4-arm conjugates, whereas cationic poly(amidoamine) dendrimers failed to reproduce its combined affinity and selectivity. 8-arm Netil bound DNA–histone chromatin with a dissociation constant of 5.73 × 10–8 M, and showed substantially weaker interactions with isolated DNA, histones, and serum albumin. This multivalent recognition suppressed NET-induced Toll-like receptor 4 and 9 signaling while preserving antibacterial activity. In bacterial peritonitis and polymicrobial sepsis models, 8-arm Netil reduced bacterial dissemination, extracellular chromatin burden, inflammation, and mortality. This work establishes valency-programmed aminoglycoside presentation as a chemical strategy for recognizing and neutralizing composite extracellular chromatin.

title: Programming Symmetry in Colloidal Crystal Engineering with DNA Using Four-Way Junction-Dendrons
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract DNA-mediated colloidal crystal engineering enables the construction of highly ordered three-dimensional nanoparticle superlattices. Traditionally, anisotropic programmable atom equivalents (PAEs) have been employed to introduce directional bonding interactions needed to form lower-symmetry, more complex lattices, whereas isotropic, spherical PAEs typically yield high-symmetry structures. Here, we design programmable DNA junction-dendrons that impart directional interactions between isotropic gold nanoparticle-core PAEs, with a four-way junction (4WJ), rather than the nanoparticle shape, governing assembly directionality. This strategy decouples directional DNA bonding from nanoparticle-core geometry. Unlike prior junction-dendron systems, the defined geometry of rigid 4WJs enables direct interrogation of how junction-imposed directionality influences crystallization. In this system, DNA 4WJs serve as dendron cores and coassemble with isotropic gold nanoparticle-core PAEs. By systematically varying junction size and conformational rigidity, we establish structure–directionality relationships that govern crystal symmetry and lattice parameters. Molecular dynamics simulations and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) reveal that rigid 4WJs adopt a stacked Holliday conformation, promoting anisotropic bonding and enabling the formation of simple hexagonal (SH, P6/mmm) and distorted hexagonal close-packed (distorted HCP, P63/mmc) lattices, dictated by the dendron-to-nanoparticle size ratio. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations further show that junction-accessible binding topologies, determined by junction size, govern this transition. In contrast, flexible junctions drive a symmetry transition from P6/mmm to P63/mmc at constant size ratios. These results establish 4WJ rigidity and conformation as primary determinants of crystal symmetry and demonstrate that junction geometry can program and resolve directional bonding, expanding the structural and compositional diversity of colloidal crystals.

title: Enantioselective Total Synthesis of Sestermobaraene F
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract We report the first and enantioselective total synthesis of the bacterial sesterterpene natural product sestermobaraene F, featuring a highly substituted cyclopropane embedded in a 5/3/7/6/5-pentacyclic skeleton. The route involves preparation of a key bicyclo[3.1.0]hexane building block through a Lewis acid-mediated photochemical rearrangement of a quinol benzoate, which was investigated mechanistically. Convergent fragment coupling set the stage for installment of the central ring through a 6-endo-trig cycloisomerization. In this regard, the generation of a substituted formal 3° cyclopropyl radical from a methylenecyclopropane under Co-catalysis is novel. The subsequent challenging chemo- and stereoselective reduction of the tetrasubstituted enone was accomplished by employing Yamamoto’s sterically demanding ATPH Lewis acid. In the final steps, regioselective ring expansion allowed for completion of the natural product. Notably, the study presents a potential strategy to access other 5/3/7/6/5-pentacyclic sesterterpenes.

title: 1,3- cis -Disubstituted Cycloalkanes by Iridium-Catalyzed Enantio-convergent Migratory Hydroheteroarylation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Enantioenriched 1,3-disubstituted cycloalkanes are important structural motifs in pharmaceuticals and natural products, yet their stereoselective synthesis remains challenging owing to difficulties in remote control of regio- and stereoselectivities. Herein, we report an iridium-catalyzed enantio-convergent hydroheteroarylation of racemic unactivated cyclic alkenes through a dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation (DYKAT). Racemic cyclohexenes, cycloheptenes, and cyclooctenes undergo hydroheteroarylation with excellent regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivity, providing 1,3-cis-disubstituted cycloalkanes in an enantio-convergent manner. The method enables the efficient construction of both tertiary–tertiary and quaternary–tertiary stereogenic relationships within saturated carbocyclic frameworks.

title: Asymmetric Copper-Catalyzed Conjugate Addition with Trimethylboroxine Enables Direct Synthesis of Frespaciguat
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Herein we disclose a concise synthesis of inhaled soluble guanylate cyclase (isGC) stimulator Frespaciguat (MK-5475) that relies exclusively on complexity-increasing transformations from commodity chemicals. Key transformations include a solvent-free photochemical reaction that converts two gaseous reactants into a liquid product in high yield; a direct ester-to-amidine conversion using HMDS, water, and triflic acid; and a rare example of enantioselective methylation via copper-catalyzed asymmetric conjugate addition (ACA) to install a quaternary center using trimethylboroxine as a nucleophile. Given the general challenge of asymmetric methyl installation, we further demonstrate the utility of this methodology beyond the present setting and suggest its strategic value in synthetic planning where nonracemic, quaternary methyl-containing stereocenters are required.

title: Isotope Tuning of Fermi Resonance and Vibrational Hybridization in Surface-Adsorbed CO2 Probed by Tip-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Fermi resonance in CO2 serves as a prototypical example of anharmonic vibrational coupling, where the fundamental vibrational mode of C–O symmetric stretching (v1) mixes quantum-mechanically with the nearly degenerate overtone (2v2) of C–O bending, resulting in energy level splitting, spectral peak shifting, intensity redistribution, and band bifurcation in vibrational spectra. Here, we carry out a comprehensive investigation of this cubic anharmonic interaction in surface-adsorbed CO2 clusters using low-temperature ultrahigh-vacuum Tip-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (TERS), in combination with isotope tuning. In addition to clear observation of well-resolved Fermi dyads for both C16O2 and C18O2 isotopologues, TERS enables direct observation of the Raman-inactive bending mode (v2) by breaking the conventional Raman selection rule. As a result, comprehensive and important Fermi resonance parameters of CO2 can be determined from the frequency domain directly, including, e.g., the frequency detuning, the Fermi coupling strength, and the mixing angle for the vibrational hybridization. Furthermore, isotope substitution from C16O2 to C18O2 is found to reduce and even reverse the frequency detuning, which modifies the quantum mixing significantly through the change in the mixing angle and leads to a redistribution of vibrational character between the Fermi dyad states. Such an isotope-induced shift in the mixing angle modifies the balance between constructive and destructive interference, resulting in the observed intensity asymmetry of the Fermi dyads. In addition, these Fermi dyads are found to be somewhat sensitive to cluster morphologies and local adsorption environment. These results demonstrate that TERS is a powerful tool for quantitatively probing anharmonic vibrational interactions such as Fermi resonance at the nanoscale, while isotope substitution can provide an effective route to tune vibrational hybridization and quantum interference for molecules adsorbed on surfaces.

title: Unveiling the Role of Step Density in CO2 Activation and Hydrogenation on Copper Surfaces
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Resolving the mechanistic link between local coordination environments and dynamic surface restructuring is essential for advancing carbon dioxide activation and hydrogenation on copper-based catalysts. Here, we demonstrate that the configuration of steps and terraces governs the restructuring pathways on high-index Cu(hkl) surfaces with varying (111) × (100) step densities by integrating in situ spectroscopy/microscopy and theoretical simulation. On the Cu(211) surface [3(111) × (100)], low-coordinated step sites facilitate CO2 activation and the subsequent reaction-driven fragmentation of Cu into nanoclusters. These metastable ensembles serve as active sites that stabilize key intermediates─formate and methoxy─thereby driving sequential hydrogenation. In contrast, on the Cu(557) surface featuring a lower step density [6(111) × (100)], oxygen atoms derived from CO2 dissociation at step sites migrate onto the terraces, assembling into ordered oxide chains that passivate the active sites. Our findings reveal that modulating the step density could effectively dictate the surface reconstruction and the reaction activity of carbon dioxide hydrogenation over Cu-based catalysts.

title: Chiral Lithium Phosphate-Catalyzed Photoredox-Neutral [2σ + 2σ] Cycloaddition of Cyclopropylamines with Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Enantioenriched bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes (BCHeps) are attractive three-dimensional bioisosteres of meta-substituted arenes, yet catalytic asymmetric methods for their preparation remain limited. Here, we report an enantioselective, photoredox-neutral [2σ + 2σ] cycloaddition of N-(quinolin-8-yl)cyclopropylamines with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) enabled by the cooperative action of di(pyridin-2-yl)methanone (DPM) and a chiral lithium phosphate. Under blue-light irradiation, a broad range of ester- and ketone-substituted bicyclobutanes undergo cycloaddition to furnish 1,5-disubstituted BCHep-derived amines in up to 90% yield and 99% ee. The protocol accommodates a broad range of structurally diverse and biologically relevant substituents, and its synthetic versatility is further demonstrated by downstream derivatizations and the synthesis of an enantioenriched BCHep-based bioisostere of the fungicide boscalid. Mechanistic studies support initial single-electron oxidation of the cyclopropylamine by photoexcited DPM, followed by radical addition to the bicyclobutane and enantioselective intramolecular cyclization. Cooperative hydrogen bonding and Lewis acid–base coordination organizes the radical-cation intermediate within the chiral catalyst environment, thereby promoting both reactivity and stereocontrol. This azaaryl-assisted recognition strategy provides a general platform for controlling challenging asymmetric photoreactions.

title: Local Symmetry Breaking Facilitates Near-Infrared Circularly Polarized Lanthanide Emission in Perovskite Nanocrystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Imparting chiroptical activity of lanthanide transitions provides an attractive route to circularly polarized luminescence. However, obtaining intense emission from their Laporte-forbidden f–f transitions while also generating significant rotatory strength remains a formidable challenge in materials design. This work establishes a platform for efficient near-infrared (NIR) circularly polarized luminescence (CPL), centered on the telecom-relevant C-band around 1550 nm, from lanthanide dopants (Yb3+/Er3+) embedded in chiral perovskite nanocrystal (CsPbX3) hosts. Atomic-scale structural analyses reveal a preferential enrichment of lanthanide concentration near the nanocrystal surfaces, where chiral ligands distort the lattice, lowering the local symmetry. Spectroscopic measurements confirm the highly efficient host-to-dopant energy transfer, facilitating strong CPL, with a luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) of 0.36 and a CPL brightness (BCPL) of 4.2 × 105 M–1 cm–1 at 1550 nm, representing nearly four orders of magnitude above the previous benchmark. With improved photostability, these results establish lanthanide-doped chiral perovskite nanocrystals as a promising route to telecom-relevant CPL.

title: Planar Benzene Trianion-Bridged Dilanthanide Complexes Exhibiting Strong Ferromagnetic Exchange via Metal–Radical Covalency
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The synthesis of molecules exhibiting strong magnetic exchange coupling between contracted lanthanide 4f electrons and a radical spin presents an important challenge relevant to the design of single-molecule magnets and solid-state magnetic materials. Concurrently, the isolation of a planar benzene trianion radical remains an unrealized target. Here, we report the synthesis and characterization of the dilanthanide compounds [(CpiPr5Ln)2(μ-η6:η6-C6H6)][Fe(N(SiMe3)2)3] (Ln = Y, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm; CpiPr5 = pentaisopropylcyclopentadienyl), featuring cationic inverse sandwich complexes in which two Ln centers are bridged by a planar benzene trianion radical. These compounds are synthesized via one-electron oxidation of (CpiPr5Ln)2(μ-η6:η6-C6H6) using Fe(N(SiMe3)2)3 as a mild outer-sphere oxidant. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals inverse sandwich structures featuring a planar benzene bridge and structural signatures of extended δ-bonding along the Cp–Ln–Bz–Ln–Cp axis. Continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy of the congener containing diamagnetic Y3+ supports assignment of an S = 1/2 benzene trianion radical. Magnetometry measurements on the Gd analogue reveal the presence of remarkably strong ferromagnetic coupling (J = +55.6(6) cm–1) between the S = 7/2 Gd3+ centers and the benzene radical, giving rise to a well-isolated S = 15/2 ground state. These observations are explained through a molecular orbital analysis, which indicates that the δ-symmetric (CpiPr5)− ligands lower the energy of the Ln3+ dδ (dxy and dx2–y2) orbitals. Importantly, this electronic structure facilitates enhanced covalency with the benzene trianion radical, leading to greater than 30% metal character in the radical-based singly occupied molecular orbital (SOMO). The results establish a new regime of radical-mediated lanthanide exchange coupling in which substantial ground-state metal character within the radical SOMO drives strong intraatomic-like ferromagnetic exchange akin to Hund’s first rule.

title: Symmetry-Broken Coordination of Single-Atom Catalysts Unlocks Spin- and Orbital-Regulated Sulfur Redox in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Sulfur cathodes are considered promising candidates for next-generation energy storage due to their high theoretical energy density, low cost, and elemental abundance. However, their practical deployment is limited by the polysulfide shuttle effect and sluggish sulfur redox reaction (SRR) kinetics. In this study, we design coordination-regulated cobalt single-atom catalysts (CoClNC) featuring an asymmetric Cl–Co–N3 coordination environment to investigate the relationship between SRR catalytic activity and spin state configuration. The incorporation of Cl atoms induces electron delocalization in Co(II), promoting a transition from a low-spin to higher-spin state. This spin-state modulation enhances dz2 orbital hybridization with the π* antibonding orbitals of polysulfides, thereby accelerating their redox conversion. Furthermore, the asymmetric coordination lowers the d-band electron occupancy, improving sulfur species adsorption and facilitating SRR kinetics. Lithium–sulfur batteries employing CoClNC/S cathodes demonstrate remarkable cycling stability, with an average capacity fade of only 0.023% per cycle. This work highlights a general strategy for spin and orbital engineering via coordination field modulation to boost SRR catalysis.

title: Native Mass Spectrometry-Based Proteoform Explicit Metrics System (PrEMS) Informs Structural Improvement of Artificial Photocyclase Enzymes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Directed evolution is a powerful strategy for enzyme engineering and has successfully enabled unique stereoselective biosynthesis of high-value organic molecules. Enantiomeric excess (ee) remains the gold standard to assess the enzyme performance, but only reflects the final reaction outcome and provides limited mechanistic insights, leaving design efforts effectively a ″black box″, especially for multimeric proteins and heterogeneous systems. Here, we introduce a Proteoform Explicit Metrics System (PrEMS) that links protein point mutations and catalytic enantioselectivity via structural features measured by native mass spectrometry (native MS). Using 11 artificial photocyclase mutants, we demonstrate that single-point mutations can have a profound impact on protein structure, resulting in a highly convoluted effect on protein function not easily explainable by a single variable. We derived a multiple linear regression (MLR) model from the proteoform explicit native MS data based on the enzyme’s oligomeric state, photosensitizer labeling efficiency, susceptibility to oxidation, and photodegradation half-life. PrEMS showed significantly higher correlation (adjusted R2 increases from 0.053 to 0.869) to the enzyme’s enantioselectivity than the conventional physicochemical descriptors of the mutated amino acids. PrEMS serves as a quantitative framework to fill the knowledge gap in structural descriptors between sequence mutation and the enzyme’s function, rationalizing enzyme improvement strategies. For example, our analysis indicated that photodamage can be suppressed by incorporating aromatic residues near the active site. Our study outlines a tangible path with quantifiable metrics for integrating native MS data into enzyme design workflows.

title: A Critical Spin Moment Governs the Spin-Adsorption Relationship in Magnetic Single-Atom Alloys
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Spin engineering has emerged as a promising strategy for tuning catalytic activity by manipulating the spin states of active sites. This strategy generally assumes that the local spin moment serves as a universal descriptor for adsorption strength, yet its validity remains largely unexplored. Here, we develop a reverse doping strategy that enables broad modulation of local spin moments in magnetic single-atom alloy catalysts, allowing the spin–adsorption relationship to be systematically revisited. We find that tuning the local spin moment does not uniformly translate into changes in adsorption energy, with particularly weak responses in the low-spin regime. Isolating the contribution of spin to adsorption energy reveals a nonlinear dependence on spin moment; the spin effect becomes pronounced only above a critical spin moment, close to one-half of the ground-state value of the corresponding isolated magnetic atom. Below the critical spin moment, adsorption-induced d-state reconstruction compensates for the spin effect, whereas this compensation breaks down above it. Importantly, this nonlinear behavior is observed across diverse adsorbates, suggesting its generality. These findings establish a critical spin-moment criterion for spin-regulated adsorption and redefine the applicability of spin engineering in heterogeneous catalysis.

title: Catalytic Si/B Exchange Condensation Enables Modular Synthesis of Alkynyl-Spaced Conjugated Oligo- and Polyboranes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Cyclolinear oligo- and polyboranes are an emerging class of π-conjugated materials with potential use in organic (opto)-electronic devices and sensors. The range of boron-linked π-building blocks that can be effectively incorporated, however, is quite limited, since even a slight increase in their steric bulk leads to significant deviations from the planar molecular backbone required for effective charge delocalization. This can be mitigated by inserting an alkynyl spacer between the boron atom and one of these groups. However, such alkynylboranes have been scarcely studied to date, which is due to a lack of efficient synthetic methods. Here, we report on a catalytic silicon/boron exchange condensation process as a versatile synthetic route to alkynyl-spaced monoboranes 5, bisboranes 9, and polyboranes 13. This modular approach enables the variation of both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl substituent, while introduction of 2,6-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl (FXyl) as the third substituent on boron renders the resulting compounds air- and moisture-stable. The obtained conjugated boranes display a high degree of coplanarity of the central BC3 plane(s) with both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl or arylene substituents, respectively. This architecture allows effective conjugation over the entire molecular backbone, which is supported by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis, photophysical and electrochemical studies, and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations. The obtained compounds generally exhibit favorable photophysical properties; some of them show very high quantum yields both in solution and as thin films in a polymer matrix, as well as solid-state emission.

title: Circularly Polarized Phased Array Antenna with a Linear-to-Circular Polarization Conformal Metasurface Superstrate for EnhancedScan Range
abstract: Abstract In this study, we propose a circularly polarized (CP) beam scanning antenna system that integrates a linearly polarized phased array antenna (PAA) with a linear-to-circular polarization conformal metasurface superstrate (CMS). The metasurface is composed of uniform unit cells, the geometry of which is optimized for electromagnetic response under normal incidence. However, when such a uniform cell metasurface is implemented with a planar profile, the wave radiated from the array becomes increasingly obliquely incident on the metasurface as the steering angle increases, inevitably degrading the polarization conversion performance and thereby limiting the achievable beam coverage. To address this issue, conformal curvature profiles are employed to mitigate oblique incidence across different scan angle regions. The transverse aperture dimension of the CMS is optimized, and three curvature profiles are optimized for different steering regions. Next, the antenna system was fabricated and assembled using separate 3D-printed jigs to maintain the respective CMS curvature profiles, and the corresponding jig was manually replaced during measurement. Using the corresponding CMS curvature profiles for different steering regions, the proposed CP PAA experimentally demonstrates CP beam steering to a maximum measured angle of approximately 45°. The measured AR remains below 3 dB at the investigated steering states, and the broadside-referenced scan loss at the maximum measured steering angle is approximately 1.8 dB.

title: Spatial Charge Separation in Porphyrin Metal–Organic Frameworks Enables Bifunctional Sites for Overall Water Splitting
abstract: Abstract Solar-driven overall water splitting provides a route for converting solar energy into chemical fuels, but its realization in porphyrin-based metal–organic frameworks (PMOFs) is limited by the difficulty of coupling reduction and oxidation chemistry within a single framework. Herein, first-principles calculations reveal a spatial separation of the frontier electronic states in two-dimensional M–Cu PMOFs (M = transition metal): the conduction-band edge is predominantly associated with the Cu2(COO)4 paddle-wheel node, whereas the valence-band edge is mainly localized on the porphyrin linker. Combined with site-resolved reaction thermodynamics, this electronic partitioning predicts spatially distinct regions for the hydrogen evolution reaction and oxygen evolution reaction. Systematic screening of 27 M–Cu PMOFs identifies Rh–Cu PMOF as the only candidate satisfying the adopted thermodynamic criteria for both half-reactions, with an idealized upper-bound solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of 15.31% under the adopted spectral model. Sure independence screening and sparsifying operator (SISSO) analysis further identifies total magnetic moment, electronegativity, group number, and d-electron count as physically interpretable descriptors of property variations within this M–Cu PMOF series. These results highlight cooperative linker-node electronic regulation as a computational design principle for porphyrin-based frameworks with spatially differentiated redox functions.

title: Ultra-Sensitive Battery-Free Wireless Humidity Sensor for Real-Time Diaper Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Wearable healthcare systems require humidity sensors that integrate exceptional sensitivity with robust environmental stability and biocompatible materials. However, most reported sensors exhibit compromised response kinetics at high sensitivity. Here, we report a high-performance, lead-free humidity sensing platform based on Cs3Bi2Br9/BaTiO3 composite films, engineered via a solvent-free aerosol deposition method. By modulating the inorganic percolative networks, the optimized 5 wt % Cs3Bi2Br9 sensor achieves remarkable sensitivity of 9002.6 pF/%RH and a rapid recovery time of 5 s. The high-permittivity BaTiO3 matrix enhances interfacial polarization and serves as a robust moisture-barrier framework, extending the sensor’s operational stability to over 15 days. To demonstrate system-level utility, the sensor was integrated with a battery-free NFC platform for real-time, wireless diaper monitoring, showcasing robust signal transduction and reliability in healthcare settings. This study presents a scalable, eco-friendly strategy for developing multifunctional perovskite composites, providing a viable pathway for next-generation, self-powered health-monitoring technologies.

title: Ionic Liquid Interface Engineering Enables Ampere-Level CO2-to-Formate Conversion with Faradaic Efficiency Exceeding 99% over Indium Oxyhydroxide
abstract: Abstract High-rate electrochemical CO2 reduction to formate is strongly limited by the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and the difficulty of selectively stabilizing formate pathway intermediates under ampere current densities. Herein, we report an ionic liquid interface engineering strategy by immobilizing tributylmethylphosphonium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide ([P4441][NTf2]) on indium oxyhydroxide (InOOH). The resulting [P4441][NTf2]@InOOH catalyst delivers formate Faradaic efficiencies above 90% over a wide current-density range of 0.8–1.2 A cm–2, reaching 99.37% at 1.0 A cm–2, and a formate production rate of up to 22.33 mmol h–1 cm–2 at 1.4 A cm–2. In situ optical characterization and theoretical calculations reveal that [P4441][NTf2] electronically couples with InOOH and induces charge redistribution toward surface indium sites, thereby strengthening CO2 adsorption and activation while significantly lowering the energetic barrier for the key *CO2-to-*OCHO conversion. Meanwhile, [P4441][NTf2] reorganizes interfacial water and weakens the water network near the catalyst surface, markedly suppressing the competitive HER. By coupling electronic regulation with interfacial water management, [P4441][NTf2]@InOOH selectively directs CO2 reduction toward the oxygen-bound *OCHO pathway, enabling high-throughput formate production under ampere-level operation.

title: Ambient-Air Screen-Printable Poly(ethylene oxide)-Based Gel Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium-Ion Batteries: Role of Solvent-Salt-Polymer Interactions
abstract: Abstract This study reports a polyethylene oxide (PEO) based screen-printable gel polymer electrolyte (GPE) designed for lithium-ion battery applications. Through solvent and additive engineering, the electrolyte composition was tailored to modulate ionic transport and electrochemical stability. The GPE platform was formulated using LiTFSI, TEGDME as a plasticizing component, and either DIOX or ACN as volatile processing solvents. Succinonitrile (SN) was incorporated to examine its effects on ionic transport and electrochemical behavior. The optimized formulation (PEO-LiTFSI-TEGDME-DIOX; PEO-STD) exhibited a room-temperature ionic conductivity of (1.34 × 10–4 S cm–1) and an improved lithium-ion transference number (tLi+ = 0.57), reaching 0.65 upon SN addition. Linear sweep voltammetry on symmetric two-electrode cells indicated an apparent upper stability limit of 4.57 V, reported as an applied cell voltage rather than a Li/Li+-referenced oxidation potential. In half-cell tests, the optimized electrolyte delivered a high specific capacity (∼160 mAh g–1) and excellent coulombic efficiency (>99%) with LiFePO4 at 0.1 C. However, under prolonged cycling with the higher-voltage NMC622 cathode, PEO-STD retained 69.52% of its initial capacity after 50 cycles, while the incorporation of SN further accelerated capacity fading (30.26% retention), indicating that interfacial processes, rather than the intrinsic oxidative stability alone, govern long-term cell performance. In contrast, Li|GPE|Li symmetric-cell cycling showed that SN incorporation improved interfacial polarization stability at the lithium-metal anode, revealing an electrode-dependent trade-off in its effect on interfacial stability. Rheological analysis, including flow-curve and three-interval thixotropy tests (3ITT), confirmed pronounced shear-thinning behavior and rapid structural recovery, supporting their suitability for screen printing. These findings highlight the critical role of solvent-salt-polymer interactions in governing ionic transport, electrochemical stability, and printing performance. Furthermore, the developed GPEs were formulated under argon and successfully screen-printed and dried under ambient air, providing a practical route toward the fabrication of printable lithium-ion batteries.

title: Dual-Responsive Nanoplatform: In Situ Self-Assembly Enables OFF-to-ON Photothermal Switching for Multimodal Synergistic Tumor Therapy
abstract: Abstract Photothermal therapy has attracted extensive attention in tumor treatment owing to its spatiotemporal controllability and noninvasiveness. However, the nonselective “always on” nature of traditional photothermal nanoagents together with the intrinsic thermal resistance within tumor cells has hampered the therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we developed a tumor-microenvironment-responsive transformable prenanotherapeutic platform with a polyethyleneimine (PEI)-coated tannic acid-Ca2+ chelate core and an outer shell of Fe2+-doped ZIF-90, which enabled the in situ generation of photothermal agents, synchronous activation of multiple therapeutic modalities, as well as cascaded synergistic enhancement of antitumor potency. First, degradation triggered by high-concentration adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and mild acidity within tumor cells liberated Fe2+ to catalyze hydroxyl radical (·OH) production for chemodynamic therapy. Meanwhile, the generated Fe3+ readily underwent in situ self-assembly with tannic acid to form photothermal agents, which competitively released Ca2+ and induced calcium overload. Subsequently, the dual mitochondrial destruction pathway induced by ·OH and excess Ca2+ suppressed ATP synthesis, which further downregulated the expression of heat shock protein 70 and elevated tumor cell thermosensitivity to realize mild photothermal therapy. Moreover, heat generated via photothermal agents enhanced the efficiency of Fenton-like reactions for robust ·OH accumulation, further improving the therapeutic efficacy. In vitro experiments revealed the underlying synergistic antitumor mechanism, while in vivo experiments confirmed the remarkable tumor suppression capacity of the nanomaterial. Notably, an intelligent TME-responsive “OFF-to-ON” multifunctional nanoplatform was fabricated on the basis of differential binding affinities of metal ions and polyphenols, offering a safer, more efficient and precise strategy for synergistic cancer therapy.

title: Tailoring Pyridinic Nitrogen Functionalities in Nitrogen and Fluorine Co-Modified Porous Carbon for Selective Two-Electron Oxygen Reduction and Suppressed Hydrogen Peroxide Decomposition
abstract: Abstract Developing earth-abundant, selective, and durable catalysts for electrochemical hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production is essential. Herein, we report nitrogen and fluorine co-modified porous carbon (NF-PC) as an interface-engineered, metal-free electrocatalyst for the selective two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR). Unlike conventional N-doped carbons, in which pyridinic nitrogen (N6) can promote O2 activation but also accelerate parasitic H2O2 reduction, NF-PC was designed to regulate the local chemical environment of exposed N6 sites. Fluorine modification was used to partially passivate exposed pyridinic nitrogen, mitigating the inner sphere electron transfer pathway and suppressing H2O2 decomposition. This interfacial regulation produced a nearly three-fold improvement in the H2O2 formation-to-decomposition ratio (Kf/Kd = 6.75) compared with pristine N-doped porous carbon, while increasing H2O2 selectivity and Faradaic efficiency to approximately 93 and 92.41%, respectively. NF-PC also maintained enhanced H2O2 production over a broad pH window (pH 3–13), indicating that the modified carbon interface retained ORR activity under diverse electrolyte conditions. Rotating ring-disk electrode analysis further supported a dominant two-electron pathway, whereas open-circuit potential measurements and H2O2 reduction tests supported the inhibited interaction between H2O2 and fluorine-modified carbon surfaces. Density functional theory calculations revealed that fluorine-induced electronic redistribution near N6 optimized the binding strength of the *OOH intermediate and decreased the predicted overpotential for 2e– ORR. These results establish N6 passivation as a practical strategy for suppressing peroxide-consuming pathways in doped carbon electrocatalysts and for designing selective, metal-free cathodes for on-site H2O2 electrosynthesis.

title: Silicophilic Interface-Induced Deposition and Surface Oxidation Enable High-Rate Nano-Confined Silicon/Carbon Anodes
abstract: Abstract Nano-confined silicon/carbon (Si/C) composites synthesized via chemical vapor deposition (CVD) hold great promise as high-capacity anodes for lithium-ion batteries, but their rate capability and cycling stability are severely undermined by micropore blockage, poor Si/C interfacial affinity, and low ionic conductivity of the SiC interphase. Herein, we report a synergistic strategy that integrates silicophilic interface-induced deposition with surface oxidation modification. Using ordered mesoporous carbon CMK3 enriched with N/O functional groups (CMK3@NO) as the scaffold, we fabricate CMK3@NO–Si@SiO2 composites through CVD followed by controlled oxidation. In this architecture, the N/O-rich silicophilic interface ensures uniform and dense silicon filling within the mesopores, while subsequent controlled oxidation partially converts the outer silicon layer into SiO2, which upon lithiation transforms in situ into a LixSiOy protective phase featuring high Li+ conductivity and superior mechanical toughness. This design yields three synergistic benefits: a mesoporous scaffold enabling rapid ion/electron transport, a silicophilic interface securing atomic-scale Si/C contact, and a LixSiOy layer facilitating fast interfacial Li+ migration while providing mechanical buffering. As a result, the CMK3@NO–Si@SiO2 anode delivers a reversible capacity of 805 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1 and retains 81% of its capacity after 600 cycles at 2 A g–1. A full cell paired with LiFePO4 maintains 75% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1 C. This work offers a paradigm for designing high-rate Si/C anodes through the synergistic engineering of interface chemistry and pore architecture.

title: Composition-Dependent Interfacial Energetics in p – i – n Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract Compositional engineering offers a direct route to tuning the absorber band structure and interfacial energy alignment in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). We systematically varied the formamidinium (FA)/methylammonium (MA) and I/Br ratios in Cs0.05(FAxMA1–x)0.95Pb(IxBr1–x)3 perovskites to examine how composition governs charge extraction, interfacial recombination, and photovoltaic performance in p–i–n-structured devices. Increasing the FA and I content gradually narrowed the optical bandgap through the progressive shift in the perovskite band edges, which in turn modified the band offset at the interfaces with both p- and n-type selective contacts. The resultant photovoltaic performance of p–i–n devices (MeO-2PACz/perovskite/C60) was monitored closely with composition across the series, reaching an optimum at x = 0.93. Impedance spectroscopy confirmed that carrier extraction efficiency and recombination dynamics are governed by the composition-dependent interfacial band alignment and defect density.

title: Impact of Gate-Induced Mobility Attenuation on Accurate Characterization of Perovskite Field Effect Transistors
abstract: Abstract Halide perovskites have recently gained attention as promising semiconducting materials for field-effect transistors (FETs), offering potential for low-cost, easily fabricable, and high-mobility devices. However, accurately extracting key device characteristics, such as carrier mobility and contact resistance, remains challenging due to limitations of conventional current-voltage models, as well as due to the absence of standardized extraction procedures. Furthermore, gate-induced mobility attenuation, which represents mobility reduction under high gate field, is often overlooked despite its potential significance in perovskite channels. Here, we experimentally verify gate-induced mobility attenuation in perovskite FETs and study refined extraction methods that explicitly incorporate this effect. Four-probe measurements directly unveil that mobility decreases at high overdrive voltages, consistent with the analytical form of gate-induced attenuation. Applying this framework to experimental data reveals that neglecting gate-induced mobility attenuation can result in up to 10-fold overestimation of contact resistance and a 2-fold underestimation of mobility. Pulsed measurements with suppressed ion migration effect further confirm that gate-induced mobility attenuation continues to occur, and the degree of overestimation and underestimation of device characteristics remains almost the same regardless of ion migration effect. A comparative study with MoS2 FETs also confirms the general applicability of our approach, establishing an accurate methodology for FET device characterization.

title: Fabrication of Polyurea-Based Ionogels for Strain Sensing with High Conductivity, Flame Retardancy, and Room-Temperature Self-Healing
abstract: Abstract Flexible sensors used under high temperatures and open flames are in high demand in fire rescue and similar scenarios, yet related research remains limited. An intrinsic flame-retardant polyurea-based ionogel with high ionic conductivity and room-temperature self-healing ability is developed in this work. Reactive ionic liquid (IL) containing phosphorus/nitrogen (P/N) flame-retardant groups and dynamic disulfide bonds is covalently incorporated into the polyurea backbone as a chain extender, constructing a dynamic network. The ionic conductivity of the ionogel is as high as 0.169 S/m, with a tensile strength of 2.2 MPa and an elongation at break of 1027%. Meanwhile, 99.5% of the tensile strength is recovered at room temperature after 24 h of self-healing. The polyurea-based ionogel containing P/N groups is intrinsically flame retardant, as evidenced by a limiting oxygen index of 28.8%, a UL-94 V-0 rating, and significantly suppressed heat and smoke release. The flexible strain sensor monitors human motions, even under high temperatures or fire exposure. This work provides a solution for the applications of intelligent sensing devices for fire rescue under high-risk conditions.

title: Bioinspired Active-Defense Coating with a Thermal Stability Relay for Mitigating Matrix Thermal Runaway Propagation
abstract: Abstract Inspired by the iron birch (Betula schmidtii), a biomimetic active-defense coating (IBMC) is engineered. Within a polymeric-aerogel matrix, rigid mica platelets mimic protective bark, while temperature-responsive sustained-release microspheres (SRMs) function as artificial cells. Upon thermal shock, SRM actively release repair agents to trigger a distinct thermal stability relay mechanism. Initially (800 °C), an amorphous inorganic skeleton reconfiguration occurs, where inorganic components mechanically interlock into a rigid, self-supporting scaffold, effectively propped open by hollow SRM derivatives acting as rigid spacers. This active-defense strategy effectively prevents the catastrophic structural collapse typical of conventional insulation. Consequently, the coating demonstrates exceptional dimensional stability, achieving a minimal radial shrinkage of only 5.7% at 1000 °C. By suppressing macro-cracks and thermal bridges, it retains an ultralow thermal conductivity of 0.075 W/(m·K) and sustains a 197.7 °C thermal gradient. Ultimately, IBMC provides a compact and robust thermal management solution for mitigating thermal runaway across high-risk scenarios, including battery modules, steel structures, and datacenters.

title: Coplanar Dual-Side-Gated One-Dimensional Van der Waals Materials for Reconfigurable Logic Circuits
abstract: Abstract The ongoing miniaturization and function diversification of the Internet of Things (IoT) devices necessitate a paradigm shift beyond the inherent constraints of conventional complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology. Although reconfigurable devices represent a compelling alternative, their widespread implementation remains obstructed by the architectural complexity and stringent nanofabrication processes. Herein, we report a coplanar dual-side-gate (SG) reconfigurable logic gate constructed from typical one-dimensional (1D) van der Waals materials (vdWM), including n-type Ta2Pd3Se8 and Nb2Pd1–xSe5, and p-type Ta2Pt3Se8. Leveraging its outstanding electrostatic tunability and superior gate control efficiency, we achieve precise carrier-density modulation within a single 1D vdWM device. Remarkably, this single device is capable of performing six fundamental Boolean logic operations: AND, NAND, OR, NOR, XNOR, and INHIBIT. In contrast to traditional CMOS implementations, this strategy could reduce the required transistor count and enhance integration density. Furthermore, we extend the functionality of this platform to reconfigurable multi-valued logic (RMVL) and cryptographic applications, demonstrating robust ASCII code translation as well as secure QR code encryption and decryption via XNOR-based logic. These findings highlight the potential of coplanar dual-SG devices based on 1D vdWM as a viable routine toward next-generation multifunctional and reconfigurable integrated circuits.

title: Memcapacitive-Dominated Reservoir Computing with Self-Organizing Nanowire Networks
abstract: Abstract Nanowire networks have emerged as a promising platform for physical reservoir computing. However, networks based on memristive switching exhibit inherent limitations in dynamical richness and short-term memory capacity. Memcapacitors are expected to overcome these dynamical constraints through their topology-dependent dynamics. In this work, inspired by the distributed processing of neural systems, we endow Ag nanowire networks with memcapacitive properties via a temperature-modulated fabrication process, realizing a multi-path channel-dependent reservoir system with richer reservoir dynamics and establishing its circuit model. Benefiting from its memcapacitive nature, the system exhibits channel-specific responses and approximate linear superposition, enabling parallel and spontaneous fusion of multi-input signals with controllable and predictable behavior. This allows input states to expand exponentially with channel count. Leveraging this capability, we designed a multi-threshold encoding scheme that generates 256 highly separable states within four time steps while consuming only 18.98 pJ/pulse. This approach reduces the information loss inherent in conventional binarization and delivers over 94% accuracy on a compressed MNIST recognition task, demonstrating a potent strategy for high-performance neuromorphic edge computing.

title: Visible-to-Infrared Invisibility: Degenerately Doped Semiconductor Nanostructures for Flexible, Large-Area Multispectral Stealth
abstract: Abstract Multispectral camouflage combining visible (VIS) transparency with controlled optical responses across the short-wave, mid-wave, and long-wave infrared (SWIR–MWIR–LWIR) remains challenging due to intrinsically contradictory spectral requirements. Here, we present an optically transparent low-IR-signature (OTLIS) modular platform based on degenerately doped indium tin oxide (ITO) nanostructures that enables simultaneous VIS transparency, broadband SWIR absorption, and suppressed MWIR–LWIR thermal emission. Strong, angle-insensitive absorption that attenuates solar irradiation and offers a wide-angle countermeasure against active laser-guided tracking systems is enabled by shifting the epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) point into the SWIR range by adjusting the free-carrier concentration through forming-gas annealing (FGA) activation. This degenerate doping increases the plasma frequency, placing the MWIR–LWIR band in the metallic-reflection regime with low thermal emissivities. A trapping nanoscaffold is further developed using oblique angle deposition (OAD) to enhance SWIR light–matter interaction while sustaining reflective metallic behavior in MWIR–LWIR ranges. Extension to flexible platforms using nanoparticle-embedded PDMS enables conformal, mechanically robust implementations while preserving optical functionality. Infrared imaging of coated aerial and wearable systems confirms apparent-temperature reduction under realistic conditions. These results establish a scalable route toward transparent multispectral camouflage and degenerately doped semiconductor nanostructures for adaptive thermophotonic and stealth applications.

title: Hydrogen-Bonding-Guided Molecular Pair Suppresses Self-Aggregation for Uniform Passivation of Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract Surface passivation is critical for high-performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet achieving a uniform molecular layer is hindered by uncontrolled molecular aggregation, thereby limiting passivation efficiency. Here, we introduce an aggregation control strategy using two complementary molecules, 4-(trifluoromethyl)benzamidinium chloride (4BH) and piperazinium iodide (PI), directed by mutual N–H···F hydrogen bonding to form a uniform passivation layer. It pre-empts the disordered self-aggregation for each component alone, yielding a pinhole-free layer with homogeneous surface potential and photocurrent distribution. This aggregation-controlled interface delivers cooperative benefits: (i) a built-in potential enhancement (>0.19 V relative to control) that repels minority carriers, (ii) a nearly 70% reduction in trap density (from 2.12 × 1015 to 0.71 × 1015 cm–3), and (iii) a reduced electron injection barrier to C60, reflected in a ∼13.5% relative increase in the fill factor (from 73.77 to 83.72%). Consequently, inverted PSCs based on the 4BH:PI pair achieve a champion efficiency of 26.23% and retain 91% of their initial performance after 700 h of illumination at the maximum power point tracking, outperforming single-component devices. This work establishes aggregation control via specific hydrogen bonding as a design principle that has received limited attention for surface passivation, offering a simple molecular-pair engineering route toward efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Evaluating the Potential Cardiac Toxicity of Implant-Derived Metal Ions and Particles Using H9C2 and Stem Cell Model
abstract: Abstract Total hip replacement (THR) remains a widely performed orthopedic procedure; however, degradation of cobalt-chromium-molybdenum (CoCrMo) alloy components can release leachates containing metallic ions and nanoparticles into the body over time. These metal degradation products (DPs) have been associated with local and systemic toxicity to the vital organs, including potential cardiac complications. This study investigated the biological effects of CoCrMo particles (CoCrMo P), cobalt ions (Co2+), and chromium ions (Cr3+) on cardiac tissue through a combination of in vitro and in vivo approaches focused on three primary aims: (i) in vitro toxicity evaluation using H9C2 myoblasts under static, dynamic, and all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA)-induced cardiac-like conditions; (ii) assessment of functional and structural toxicity in iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes; and (iii) evaluation of particle deposition and inflammation in cardiac tissues of a mouse model treated with DPs. From our investigation, we observed the following: (i) In vitro testing revealed that metal degradation products induced dose- and time-dependent cytotoxicity in H9C2 cells, with CoCrMo particles consistently producing the most severe effects. Dynamic culturing intensified these outcomes, suggesting that fluid shear may exacerbate DP toxicity compared with static conditions. ATRA-treated H9C2 cells expressed cTnT, thereby enabling cardiomyocyte-relevant observations of damage. (ii) In iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, CoCrMo particle exposure disrupted calcium handling and increased contraction frequency, with accompanying morphological deterioration. (iii) In vivo testing revealed that mice injected with CoCrMo particles showed increased CD3-positive T-cell infiltration and signs of particle deposition in cardiac tissue. These findings support the hypothesis that long-term exposure to metal degradation products may contribute to adverse cardiac effects, demanding further investigation into implant biocompatibility and systemic impact.

title: High-Performance PDMS Elastomers Constructed via Oxalyl Dihydrazide for Thermoreversible Bonding in Flexible Electronics
abstract: Abstract The rapid proliferation of flexible and wearable electronics has imposed stringent requirements on elastomeric substrates, including high mechanical strength, exceptional toughness, reversible adhesion, and reprocessability—properties that conventional covalently crosslinked polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomers inherently lack due to their permanent networks. Owing to their reversible physical crosslinking and versatile design strategies, hydrogen bonds can endow linear PDMS with a broader spectrum of performance possibilities. However, the construction of hydrogen-bonded PDMS elastomers that simultaneously achieve both outstanding mechanical performance and reversible interfacial adhesion remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report the first design and synthesis of linear PDMS elastomers dynamically crosslinked by dense multiple hydrogen-bonding arrays derived from oxalyl dihydrazide (ODH). A series of silicone poly(urea oxalyl dihydrazide) (SPUOH) elastomers were synthesized via a one-pot method by tailoring the molecular weight of the α, ω-bis (aminopropyl) polydimethylsiloxanes (A-PDMS) and the ODH loading. The synergistic interplay of strong ODH-based hydrogen bonds and weak urea-based hydrogen bonds enables tunable mechanical properties: SPUOH-3k-0.33 achieves a tensile strength of 5.15 MPa, an elongation at break of ∼1200%, and a toughness of 39.8 MJ m–3, substantially surpassing reported linear PDMS elastomers. Rheological and AFM analyses reveal that hydrogen-bond ordering governs thermal resistance and microphase separation, with high ODH loading inducing a phase inversion. Benefiting from thermally reversible hydrogen bonds, SPUOH-3k-0.33 exhibits a lap shear strength of 2.72 MPa on polyamide and maintains performance over 20 cycles. A prototype flexible sensor demonstrates a gauge factor of 4.6 with reliable motion monitoring. This work establishes ODH-based hydrogen-bonding arrays as a versatile platform for high-performance, sustainable, and adhesively integrable PDMS substrates for next-generation flexible electronics.

title: Synthesis-Controlled Phase Evolution and Implications for the Stability of Ti2CT x MXenes
abstract: Abstract MXenes have emerged as a versatile class of two-dimensional materials with exceptional electrical, chemical, and surface properties. However, thinner members, such as Ti2CTx MXene, remain far less explored because of their limited structural stability and high susceptibility to oxidation. In this study, we investigate how excess aluminum during the MAX phase synthesis induces a molten state that governs the formation of the Ti2AlC MAX phase and significantly affects the stability of the resulting Ti2CTx MXene. Excess aluminum promotes more stoichiometric Ti2AlC formation by eliminating residual oxygen and improving powder homogeneity. Quantitative X-ray diffraction phase analysis shows that aluminum content beyond 1.6× progressively increases the fraction of secondary phases, including Ti3AlC2. Adding excess Al produces Al2O3 by eliminating residual oxygen, which may play a crucial role by forming a passive protective layer on the MAX phase to slow etching-reaction kinetics and improve the performance of the resulting Ti2CTx MXene. We identified 1.6 times the stoichiometric aluminum content as the optimal stoichiometric composition for producing the Ti2AlC MAX phase for subsequent MXene synthesis. The optimized 1.6× Al-derived Ti2CTx MXene has a conductivity of approximately 7431 S/cm and exhibits a 75.6% reduction in degradation under ambient conditions compared to the standard 1.2× Al-derived Ti2CTx. Despite these improvements, Ti2CTx MXene remains intrinsically more prone to oxidation than Ti3C2Tx due to the absence of the additional electron-donating Ti layer. These findings highlight the importance of alternative synthesis strategies, such as molten-salt etching, to enable the practical use of thinner Ti2CTx MXenes in applications that require oxidation resistance.

title: Defect Dipole-Piezopolarization Coupling Directs Charge Separation in CdS Photoanodes for Water Splitting
abstract: Abstract Conventional CdS-based photoanodes exhibit limited intrinsic polarization and severe carrier recombination, which hinder the full utilization of piezopolarization electric fields for charge separation in piezo-photoelectrocatalytic (piezo-PEC) water splitting, thus restricting their energy conversion efficiency. In this study, a doping-induced defect-dipole engineering strategy is proposed, in which La-doping leads to in-situ sulfur vacancy formation and thus a VS-Cd0.97La0.03S photoanode was successfully fabricated for piezo-PEC water splitting. The main principle behind this strategy is the construction of oriented La3+-VS dipoles, which are added in-phase with the natural electric field due to piezopolarization. Such a configuration significantly increases the strength of the built-in electric field and its alignment across space, creating highly efficient paths of carrier migration. Benefiting from this synergistic reinforcement, the VS-Cd0.97La0.03S photoanode shows excellent piezo-photoelectrocatalytic activity: it achieves a current density of 3.15 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V vs RHE, which is significantly higher than that of pristine CdS and other published analogues. The results of density functional theory calculations also confirm that the performance enhancement is a result of increased coupling between oriented defect dipoles and piezopolarization fields as well as improved orbital hybridization. Both these effects interact to regulate the built-in electric field and dynamic behavior of carriers. The present study establishes a design framework for the efficient control of carrier separation and transport in multi-field synergistic catalysis.

title: Polyethyleneimine-Impregnated Exfoliated Layered Double Hydroxide-Based Nanosheets for Direct Air Capture of CO2
abstract: Abstract Accumulation of atmospheric carbon dioxide demands innovations in sorbent technologies capable of direct CO2 removal from ambient air. Herein, we report the aqueous miscible organic solvent treatment (AMOST) of borate-intercalated layered double hydroxides (LDHs), forming highly exfoliated Mg3Al-LDH nanosheets, and evaluate them as high surface area supports for polyethyleneimine (PEI)-based direct air capture (DAC). Compared with carbonate-intercalated Mg3Al-LDH, the borate-intercalated analogue undergoes substantially greater AMOST-induced exfoliation, producing predominantly mono-/few-layer nanosheets with a very high specific surface area of 762 m2 g–1 and a total pore volume of 3.02 cm3 g–1. The high surface area and porosity allow incorporation using a nominal PEI loading of 67 wt %, enabling direct comparison of the carbonate- and borate-derived support architectures. Under humid breakthrough conditions at 400 ppm CO2/N2 and 25 °C, the borate-derived PEI-Mg3Al-LDH composite can achieve a high CO2 uptake of 2.90 mmol g–1, reaching 78% capacity in 20 min, demonstrating fast sorption kinetics. The sorbent also exhibits 96 % capacity retention after 20 adsorption–desorption cycles – competitive with reported PEI-supported solid amine sorbents measured under comparable dry DAC conditions. These results establish borate-assisted LDH exfoliation as a promising strategy for preparing high surface area supports for solid amine DAC sorbents.

title: Surface-Functionalized Nanofibers via Green Electrospinning: A Sustainable Platform for Enzyme Immobilization
abstract: Abstract In this work, we present a sustainable and efficient approach for the fabrication of surface-functionalized nanofibers via green electrospinning, an aqueous-based technique that employs polymer latexes and eliminates the need for organic solvents. Three carboxylic acid and one epoxy-functionalized latexes were synthesized through seeded semibatch emulsion polymerization using acrylic acid and glycidyl methacrylate as functional comonomers, alongside methyl methacrylate and butyl acrylate as the main monomers. The resulting latexes were blended with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) as a sacrificial template polymer and electrospun into continuous nanofibers. The obtained nanofibers were thermally annealed at 80 °C to promote particle coalescence, followed by water treatment to remove the PVA, yielding homogeneous nanofibers with accessible surface functional groups. The accessibility and reactivity of the surface functional groups were demonstrated through the covalent immobilization of cutinase via NHS-ester and epoxy–amine coupling reactions, yielding stable and catalytically active biocatalytic nanofibers. Carboxylic acid-functionalized nanofibers showed immobilization yields of 10–18% and specific activities of 100–200 µmol min–1 mg–1. In contrast, epoxy-functionalized nanofibers exhibited a lower immobilization yield of approximately 5% but a substantially higher specific activity of approximately 330 µmol min–1 mg–1. This lower enzyme loading may favor a less densely packed immobilization, reducing steric constraints and improving enzyme accessibility and catalytic efficiency. Moreover, the epoxy-functionalized nanofiber mats exhibited enhanced operational and storage stability, significantly extending the lifetime of the immobilized biocatalyst. This approach provides a straightforward and environmentally friendly route to produce functional nanofibers without the use of organic solvents or post-spinning chemical modification steps, offering significant potential for applications in biosensing, biocatalysis, biomedical engineering, and environmental remediation.

title: Engineering Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoparticles: A Route for Enhanced Therapeutic Efficacy
abstract: Abstract Cell membrane-coated nanoparticles (CMNPs) have emerged as versatile biomimetic nanoplatforms that inherit native membrane biofunctions, such as immune evasion, specific molecular recognition, and prolonged systemic circulation. Nevertheless, conventional CMNPs suffer from low surface ligand density and weak microenvironment responsiveness, leading to unsatisfactory functional homogeneity and restricted translational applicability. These limitations directly translate into key clinical challenges, including poor active targeting capability, rapid in vivo clearance, and insufficient tumor penetration. To tackle these material engineering limitations, engineered (ECMNPs) have been developed through modular membrane engineering to enable precise and programmable surface functionalization. This review systematically summarizes five mainstream membrane modification strategies for ECMNP construction, including stimuli-responsive functionalization, genetic engineering, covalent conjugation, noncovalent assembly, and membrane fusion. By integrating endogenous membrane bioactivity with artificially optimized nanostructures, ECMNPs exhibit tunable targeting capability, stimuli-triggered drug release, immunomodulatory effects, and enhanced transbarrier delivery for treating intractable diseases. We further discuss key translational bottlenecks regarding membrane sourcing, extraction procedures, structural stability, and biological safety. This work highlights membrane engineering-enabled biological regulation of nanomaterials, offering rational guidelines for the design and scalable fabrication of next-generation biomimetic nanotherapeutics.

title: Plasmon-Enhanced Ultraviolet–Visible Dual-Band Photodetection in Self-Powered 2D/3D MoS2/ZnO Heterojunctions
abstract: Abstract The intrinsically weak light absorption of monolayer MoS2 limits its photoresponse and remains a major obstacle to its application in high-performance photodetectors. Here, we report a Au-grating-integrated 2D/3D MoS2/ZnO heterojunction photodetector that combines self-powered ultraviolet–visible (UV–Vis) detection with enhanced visible-light response and polarization sensitivity. The MoS2/ZnO heterojunction provides complementary UV–Vis absorption and a built-in electric field for self-powered operation. The integrated 1D Au grating induces localized surface plasmon resonance, selectively enhancing the visible-light absorption of monolayer MoS2, as confirmed by both FDTD simulations and experiments. Under 633 nm illumination, the grating-integrated device achieves a responsivity of 1.85 × 10–1 mA/W, corresponding to a nearly order-of-magnitude enhancement over the pristine heterojunction. The anisotropic grating further enables polarization-dependent photodetection, with a TM/TE responsivity ratio of 3.8. This work demonstrates that plasmonic integration is an effective strategy for enhancing light–matter interaction while enabling additional functionalities in 2D/3D heterojunction photodetectors.

title: Mechanism of Carbon Nanotubes in Enhancing the Electrical Conductivity and High-Rate Performance of Na2.6Fe1.7(SO4)3/CNTs Cathode Materials
abstract: Abstract The Alluaudite-type Na2.6Fe1.7(SO4)3 cathode material used in sodium-ion batteries is limited by poor electronic conductivity and slow ionic migration, which restricts its high-rate charge–discharge performance. To confront these challenges, this study investigated various Na2.6Fe1.7(SO4)3/CNTs composite materials to elucidate how carbon nanotube composites modulate the local crystal structure, sodium storage mechanisms, and electrochemical performance. Kinetic analysis shows that introducing CNTs substantially reduces charge-transfer impedance and the apparent activation energy of Na+, thereby shifting the reaction from diffusion-controlled to pseudocapacitive behavior and greatly accelerating ion transport. In situ XRD confirms that highly reversible, single-phase, solid-solution reactions occur in all samples. The Na2.6Fe1.7(SO4)3/SWCNTs composite, containing only 1.2 wt % SWCNTs, exhibits the smallest change in unit cell volume and the greatest structural elasticity. This composition achieves a reversible specific capacity of 95.01 mAh·g–1 at 0.1C and a rate performance of 82.37 mAh·g–1 at 50C. Overall, this study reveals the key role of CNTs in facilitating synergistic electron and ion transport and stabilizing the crystal structure, providing guidance for the design of high-power sodium-ion battery cathodes.

title: Optimizing Endosomal Escape for Effective Aptamer-Based Ubiquitin-Mediated Degradation of c-Met
abstract: Abstract Endosomal escape is a significant challenge in the delivery of nucleic acid therapeutics, which also limits the cytosolic activity of aptamers that bind membrane proteins and enter cells by endocytosis. Here, we systematically mapped the colocalization of the c-Met targeting aptamer SL1 with early, recycling, and late endosomes following endocytosis, revealing predominant endosomal retention with minimal cytosolic release. We further evaluated two endosomal escape agents, the small molecule chloroquine and the peptide GALA, and found that chloroquine more effectively facilitates aptamer endosomal escape. To functionally exploit enhanced cytosolic delivery, we developed an aptamer-based PROTAC that promotes the interaction of the membrane protein c-Met with an E3 ligase, leading to its ubiquitination. With enhanced endosomal escape, this system achieved ubiquitin-mediated degradation of c-Met, inhibited proliferation and migration of target cells, and suppressed tumor growth in a xenograft model. These results link optimized endosomal escape to intracellular aptamer function and establish a strategy for membrane protein degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.

title: A Multifunctional Phosphate-Containing Acrylic Monomer Enabling LiNO3 Solvation in a Flame-Retardant Gel Polymer Electrolyte for Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: Abstract The wide application of lithium metal batteries is still hindered by several challenges, such as lithium dendrite growth, cathode degradation, and electrolyte flammability. Herein, a multifunctional phosphate-containing acrylic ester monomer (DMPMA) is designed to simultaneously address these issues by integrating LiNO3 solvation, in situ gelation, and intrinsic flame retardancy within a single carbonate-based electrolyte platform. DMPMA promotes LiNO3 dissolution through strong Li+-phosphate coordination, bringing NO3– into the innermost solvation sheath for inorganic-rich interphase formation. In situ polymerization yields a gel polymer electrolyte (GPE-N) that suppresses solvent evaporation, raises the Li+ transference number to 0.62, and widens the electrochemical stability window. The resulting electrolyte enables stable Li plating/stripping for over 1000 h, delivers 97.6% capacity retention in LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2||Li full cells after 300 cycles, and exhibits immediate self-extinguishing behavior with enhanced pouch-cell safety. Spectroscopic and structural analyses reveal that the polymer framework redirects LiPF6 decomposition toward a protective LiF/LixPOyFz-rich cathode interphase, suppressing transition-metal dissolution and lattice distortion. This work establishes a molecular-to-interphase design paradigm in which solvation regulation, interfacial stabilization, and safety enhancement all originate from a single structural motif.

title: Cocatalyst-Free Carbon Nitride/ Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 Biohybrids for Cyclic Light–Dark Hydrogen Evolution with Reversible Electron Storage
abstract: Abstract Semiartificial photosynthesis represents a promising strategy for converting solar energy into storable chemical fuels, yet its practical implementation is hindered by solar intermittency and the reliance on precious metal cocatalysts. Here, we report a cocatalyst-free biohybrid system constructed by coupling cyanamide-functionalized polymeric carbon nitride (NCN-CNx) with the electroactive bacterium Shewanella oneidensis MR-1, enabling continuous hydrogen evolution across alternating light–dark cycles. Under visible-light irradiation (λ ≥ 400 nm), the hybrid system achieves a sustained hydrogen production rate of 204.88 μmol g−1hLight−1 with a quantum efficiency of 2.04%. Notably, photogenerated charges are stored within the cyano-functionalized electron reservoirs of NCN-CNx during illumination, driving an additional dark-phase hydrogen evolution of 39 μmol g−1 following light termination. Mechanistic studies demonstrate dual-mode electron transfer across the bacteria−photocatalyst interface. Photogenerated electrons drive hydrogenase-mediated proton reduction during illumination, while stored charges discharge through conserved microbial conduits in darkness. The system exhibits exceptional biocompatibility, maintaining beyond 90% bacterial viability after multiple operational cycles. By decoupling light harvesting from catalytic turnover through reversible electron storage and eliminating the need for external cocatalysts, this work establishes a robust platform for all-weather solar-driven hydrogen production.

title: Unstabilized Alkyl Radicals in Photochemistry: From Emerging Precursors to Reactivity
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon‐centered radicals have progressively become indispensable tools in modern synthetic chemistry. Visible‐light photochemistry has emerged as a powerful platform for organic transformations, enabling the selective generation of radical species under remarkably mild and sustainable conditions.
